          "statement": "Use the complex field $\\mathbb C$ with conjugation $z\\mapsto\\overline z$. Fix an integer $N\\ge1$. Let $S=\\mathbb C^2$ have standard basis $s_1,s_2$. For a complex vector space $W$, its conjugate vector space $\\overline W$ consists of symbols $\\overline w$ for $w\\in W$, with addition $\\overline w+\\overline v=\\overline{w+v}$ and scalar action $\\lambda\\overline w=\\overline{\\overline\\lambda w}$. Set $\\dot S=\\overline S$ with dotted basis $\\dot s_{\\dot1}=\\overline{s_1}$ and $\\dot s_{\\dot2}=\\overline{s_2}$. Let $F=\\mathbb C^N$ have standard basis $f_1,\\ldots,f_N$, and let $F^*$ be its complex-linear dual with dual basis $f^1,\\ldots,f^N$ and scalar action $(\\lambda\\ell)(v)=\\lambda\\ell(v)$. All tensor products are over $\\mathbb C$, with scalar action $\\lambda(v\\otimes w)=(\\lambda v)\\otimes w=v\\otimes(\\lambda w)$ and product bases formed from the displayed bases. Define $\\Lambda^2F=(F\\otimes_{\\mathbb C}F)/\\operatorname{span}_{\\mathbb C}\\{v\\otimes v:v\\in F\\}$; its basis is $f_I\\wedge f_J$ for $1\\le I<J\\le N$, with quotient scalar action. Its conjugate $\\overline{\\Lambda^2F}$ has basis $\\overline{f_I\\wedge f_J}$ and the conjugate scalar action just defined. For $N=1$ these exterior-square spaces are zero. In the displayed bases, $\\mathfrak{sl}(S)=\\{A\\in\\operatorname{End}_{\\mathbb C}(S):\\operatorname{tr}A=0\\}$ and $\\mathfrak{sl}(\\dot S)=\\{B\\in\\operatorname{End}_{\\mathbb C}(\\dot S):\\operatorname{tr}B=0\\}$. Put $\\epsilon_{12}=\\epsilon_{\\dot1\\dot2}=1$ and $\\epsilon_{21}=\\epsilon_{\\dot2\\dot1}=-1$, with zero diagonal. The complex even space is\n\n$$\\mathfrak g_{\\bar0}=\\bigl(\\mathfrak{sl}(S)\\oplus\\mathfrak{sl}(\\dot S)\\bigr)\\oplus V\\oplus C_N,\\qquad V=S\\otimes\\dot S,\\qquad C_N=\\Lambda^2F\\oplus\\overline{\\Lambda^2F}.$$\n\nWrite $T_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta}=s_\\alpha\\otimes\\dot s_{\\dot\\beta}$ for the basis of $V$. The listed central generators form a basis of $C_N$: $Z^{IJ}$ corresponds to $f_I\\wedge f_J$ and $\\bar Z_{IJ}$ to $\\overline{f_I\\wedge f_J}$ for $1\\le I<J\\le N$; extend them by antisymmetry in the flavor indices and set their diagonal entries to zero. The complex odd space is\n\n$$\\mathfrak g_{\\bar1}=(S\\otimes F)\\oplus(\\dot S\\otimes F^*),$$\n\nwith basis $Q^I_\\alpha=s_\\alpha\\otimes f_I$ and $\\bar Q_{\\dot\\alpha I}=\\dot s_{\\dot\\alpha}\\otimes f^I$. A homogeneous vector has parity $|x|\\in\\{0,1\\}$. The bracket is complex-bilinear, preserves parity, and obeys $[x,y]=-(-1)^{|x||y|}[y,x]$. Its complete nonzero table, apart from the graded-skew consequences, is\n\n$$[ (A,B),(A',B') ]=([A,A'],[B,B']),\\qquad [(A,B),T]= (A\\otimes I+I\\otimes B)T,$$\n\n$$[(A,B),Q^I_\\alpha]=A^\\gamma{}_{\\alpha}Q^I_\\gamma,\\qquad [(A,B),\\bar Q_{\\dot\\alpha I}]=B^{\\dot\\gamma}{}_{\\dot\\alpha}\\bar Q_{\\dot\\gamma I},$$\n\nHere $A^\\gamma{}_{\\alpha}$ is the entry in row $\\gamma$, column $\\alpha$, so $As_\\alpha=\\sum_\\gamma A^\\gamma{}_{\\alpha}s_\\gamma$; dotted entries use the same convention. Thus on the translation basis the tensor action is $[(A,B),T_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta}]=\\sum_\\gamma A^\\gamma{}_{\\alpha}T_{\\gamma\\dot\\beta}+\\sum_{\\dot\\gamma}B^{\\dot\\gamma}{}_{\\dot\\beta}T_{\\alpha\\dot\\gamma}$.\n\n$$\\{Q^I_\\alpha,\\bar Q_{\\dot\\beta J}\\}=-2\\delta^I{}_J T_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta},\\qquad \\{Q^I_\\alpha,Q^J_\\beta\\}=2\\epsilon_{\\alpha\\beta}Z^{IJ},\\qquad \\{\\bar Q_{\\dot\\alpha I},\\bar Q_{\\dot\\beta J}\\}=2\\epsilon_{\\dot\\alpha\\dot\\beta}\\bar Z_{IJ}.$$\n\nAll other brackets vanish: $V$ and $C_N$ are abelian, $C_N$ is central, and $V$ brackets trivially with the odd space. The two antisymmetric factors in each equal-chirality odd bracket make that bracket symmetric in the combined spinor-flavor labels. The Lie-superalgebra and real-form properties are established by the local Jacobi result.\n\nDefine a conjugate-linear involution $*$ on the generators by\n\n$$ (A,B)^*=(-\\overline B,-\\overline A),\\quad Q^I_\\alpha{}^*=\\bar Q_{\\dot\\alpha I},\\quad \\bar Q_{\\dot\\alpha I}{}^*=Q^I_\\alpha,\\quad T_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta}^*=T_{\\beta\\dot\\alpha},\\quad (Z^{IJ})^*=\\bar Z_{IJ},\\quad (\\bar Z_{IJ})^*=Z^{IJ}.$$\n\nIt uses the operator-adjoint convention $[x,y]^*=-(-1)^{|x||y|}[x^*,y^*]$. The associated real Lie superalgebra is the fixed space of the conjugate-linear map $\\tau(x)=-x^*$ on even elements and $\\tau(x)=i x^*$ on odd elements. Its real Lorentz algebra is the fixed diagonal copy of $\\mathfrak{sl}(2,\\mathbb C)$; its real translation generators are the $\\tau$-fixed skew-Hermitian bispinors. The star-fixed translation coordinates defined below are abstract elements of the complex algebra; their multiples by $i$ form a real basis of the tau-fixed translation space.\n\nFor the metric convention $\\eta=\\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, put $\\sigma^0=I_2$ and\n\n$$\\sigma^1=\\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\\\1&0\\end{pmatrix},\\qquad \\sigma^2=\\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\\\i&0\\end{pmatrix},\\qquad \\sigma^3=\\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\\\0&-1\\end{pmatrix},\\qquad \\bar\\sigma^0=I_2,\\qquad \\bar\\sigma^j=-\\sigma^j.$$\n\nThey obey\n\n$$\\sigma^\\mu\\bar\\sigma^\\nu+\\sigma^\\nu\\bar\\sigma^\\mu=-2\\eta^{\\mu\\nu}I_2.$$\n\nDefine abstract translation coordinates $p_0=(T_{1\\dot1}+T_{2\\dot2})/2$, $p_1=(T_{1\\dot2}+T_{2\\dot1})/2$, $p_2=(T_{2\\dot1}-T_{1\\dot2})/(2i)$, and $p_3=(T_{1\\dot1}-T_{2\\dot2})/2$. Then $T_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta}=\\sigma^\\mu_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta}p_\\mu$, $p_\\mu^*=p_\\mu$, and $\\tau(ip_\\mu)=ip_\\mu$. A representation of the complex supertranslation algebra $\\mathfrak t=V\\oplus C_N\\oplus\\mathfrak g_{\\bar1}$ on a graded complex vector space $\\mathcal D$ means a parity-preserving complex-linear map $\\rho:\\mathfrak t\\to\\operatorname{End}_{\\mathbb C}(\\mathcal D)$ preserving the bracket, where the target bracket on homogeneous endomorphisms is $[X,Y]=XY-(-1)^{|X||Y|}YX$. Write $P_\\mu=\\rho(p_\\mu)$ and use the charge symbols for their images. Thus $\\rho(T_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta})=\\sigma^\\mu_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta}P_\\mu$ and the represented mixed relation is $\\{Q^I_\\alpha,\\bar Q_{\\dot\\beta J}\\}=-2\\sigma^\\mu_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta}P_\\mu\\delta^I{}_J$, with $P_\\mu=\\eta_{\\mu\\nu}P^\\nu$. Complex linearity gives $\\rho(ip_\\mu)=iP_\\mu$, hence $-i\\rho(ip_\\mu)=P_\\mu$. For a real number $M>0$, a massive rest module here means such a supertranslation representation with $P^0=M I_{\\mathcal D}$ and $P^j=0$ for $j=1,2,3$. Consequently $P_0=-M I_{\\mathcal D}$ and its mixed anticommutator is $2M\\delta_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta}\\delta^I{}_J I_{\\mathcal D}$. This is an algebraic specialization, with no assertion of a Hilbert adjoint or a spectral fiber. Here $N$ counts left Weyl spinors; the scalar central-charge matrix is antisymmetric and therefore vanishes for $N=1$. Tensorial or topological extensions are outside this scalar-central-charge algebra. The convention uses natural units $\\hbar=c=1$; translation and central-charge generators have mass dimension one and supercharges have mass dimension one-half.",

          "statement": "For $N\\ge1$, take $S=\\mathbb C^2$, $\\dot S=\\overline S$, $\\mathfrak l=\\mathfrak{sl}(S)\\oplus\\mathfrak{sl}(\\dot S)$, $V=S\\otimes\\dot S$, $C_N=\\Lambda^2\\mathbb C^N\\oplus\\overline{\\Lambda^2\\mathbb C^N}$, even part $\\mathfrak g_{\\bar0}=\\mathfrak l\\oplus V\\oplus C_N$, and odd part $\\mathfrak g_{\\bar1}=(S\\otimes\\mathbb C^N)\\oplus(\\dot S\\otimes(\\mathbb C^N)^*)$.           "statement": "Assume Countable Choice. Use the complex Hilbert-space convention that the inner product is linear in its first variable and conjugate-linear in its second. Let $\\eta=\\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $\\sigma^0=I_2$, $\\sigma^1=\\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\\\1&0\\end{pmatrix}$, $\\sigma^2=\\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\\\i&0\\end{pmatrix}$, and $\\sigma^3=\\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\\\0&-1\\end{pmatrix}$. Define $\\operatorname{Herm}_2(\\mathbb C)=\\{H\\in M_2(\\mathbb C):H^\\dagger=H\\}$ and $\\Phi:\\mathbb R^{1,3}\\to\\operatorname{Herm}_2(\\mathbb C)$ by $\\Phi(x)=-\\sigma^\\mu x_\\mu$. For $g\\in\\mathrm{SL}(2,\\mathbb C)=\\{g\\in M_2(\\mathbb C):\\det g=1\\}$, define $\\Lambda_g$ by $\\Phi(\\Lambda_gx)=g\\Phi(x)g^\\dagger$; the real-linear map $\\Phi$ is an isomorphism because $I_2,\\sigma^1,\\sigma^2,\\sigma^3$ form a basis of $\\operatorname{Herm}_2(\\mathbb C)$. Since $\\det g=1$, $\\det(g\\Phi(x)g^\\dagger)=\\det g\\,\\det\\Phi(x)\\,\\overline{\\det g}=\\det\\Phi(x)$; with $\\det\\Phi(x)=-\\eta_{\\mu\\nu}x^\\mu x^\\nu$, this proves determinant and Lorentz-form preservation. These maps satisfy $\\Lambda_{I_2}=I$ and $\\Lambda_g\\Lambda_h=\\Lambda_{gh}$: applying $\\Phi$ to the left side gives $gh\\Phi(x)h^\\dagger g^\\dagger=(gh)\\Phi(x)(gh)^\\dagger$, and injectivity of $\\Phi$ gives the equality; in particular $\\Lambda_{g^{-1}}=\\Lambda_g^{-1}$. Thus $g\\mapsto\\Lambda_g$ is a group action, so it defines the semidirect-product structure below. Congruence by $g$ preserves positive-semidefinite Hermitian matrices, so $\\Lambda_g$ preserves the chosen future cone. Let $\\Lambda_g^\\vee$ be the dual action on covectors, $(\\Lambda_g^\\vee p)(x)=p(\\Lambda_g^{-1}x)$. The spin-cover Poincare group is $\\mathcal P=\\mathrm{SL}(2,\\mathbb C)\\ltimes_\\Lambda\\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with product $(g,a)(h,b)=(gh,a+\\Lambda_gb)$.\n\nA **positive unitary super-Poincare representation** in this item is the following data. It includes a nonzero complex Hilbert space $\\mathcal H$ and a bounded self-adjoint grading operator $\\Gamma$ with $\\Gamma^2=I$; write $\\mathcal H^\\pm=\\ker(\\Gamma\\mp I)$. Give $\\mathcal P=\\mathrm{SL}(2,\\mathbb C)\\ltimes_\\Lambda\\mathbb R^{1,3}$ the product topology from the usual matrix topology and Euclidean topology. Let $\\mathcal U(\\mathcal H)=\\{V\\in\\mathcal B(\\mathcal H):V^*V=VV^*=I\\}$. The data include a map $U:\\mathcal P\\to\\mathcal U(\\mathcal H)$ satisfying $U(1,0)=I$ and $U((g,a)(h,b))=U(g,a)U(h,b)$ for all $(g,a),(h,b)\\in\\mathcal P$, with $U(g,a)\\Gamma=\\Gamma U(g,a)$. Require the orbit map $(g,a)\\mapsto U(g,a)\\psi$ to be norm-continuous for every $\\psi\\in\\mathcal H$; this is strong continuity. The data also include a regular projection-valued measure $E$ on the Borel subsets of the covector space $(\\mathbb R^{1,3})^*$ such that\n\n$$U(1,a)=\\Phi_E(p\\mapsto e^{i p(a)}),\\qquad U(g,0)E(B)U(g,0)^*=E(\\Lambda_g^\\vee B),\\qquad E(\\mathcal C_+^*)=I,$$\n\nwhere $\\Phi_E$ is the bounded Borel PVM integral, $\\mathcal C_+^*=\\{p:p^0=-p_0\\ge |\\vec p|\\}$ is the closed future cone in covector coordinates, and $p(a)=p_\\mu a^\\mu$. The PVM functional calculus makes every translation unitary commute with every $E(B)$. For each coordinate define the self-adjoint translation generator\n\n$$P_\\mu=p_\\mu(E),\\qquad D(P_\\mu)=\\left\\{\\psi\\in\\mathcal H:\\int |p_\\mu|^2\\,dE_\\psi(p)<\\infty\\right\\},\\qquad E_\\psi(B)=\\langle E(B)\\psi,\\psi\\rangle.$$\n\nHere $p_\\mu(E)$ is the unbounded PVM integral with its truncation domain; the real-valued integral is self-adjoint under Countable Choice. Thus $P^0=\\eta^{0\\nu}P_\\nu$ is nonnegative. The joint PVM is part of the representation data; no joint spectral measure is inferred from formal commutators on a dense domain.\n\nFor each $I,\\alpha$, the supercharge $Q^I_\\alpha$ is a closed densely defined operator on $\\mathcal H$ and $\\bar Q_{\\dot\\alpha I}=(Q^I_\\alpha)^*$ is its actual Hilbert adjoint, with exactly the adjoint domain. Require the grading to preserve each actual charge domain and each closed charge to be odd there: $\\Gamma D(Q^I_\\alpha)=D(Q^I_\\alpha)$ and $Q^I_\\alpha\\Gamma\\psi=-\\Gamma Q^I_\\alpha\\psi$ for every $\\psi\\in D(Q^I_\\alpha)$, with the same two conditions for $(Q^I_\\alpha)^*$ on $D((Q^I_\\alpha)^*)$. The central generators $Z^{IJ}$ and $\\bar Z_{IJ}$, which belong to the even part of the algebra, are represented by closed densely defined operators with $\\bar Z_{IJ}=(Z^{IJ})^*$ as an actual Hilbert adjoint; require $\\Gamma D(Z^{IJ})=D(Z^{IJ})$ and $Z^{IJ}\\Gamma\\psi=\\Gamma Z^{IJ}\\psi$ on $D(Z^{IJ})$, with the corresponding conditions for $\\bar Z_{IJ}$ on its actual domain. On a common dense graded linear domain $\\mathcal D$, contained in the domains of every generator product in the bracket table, the operator supercommutator is the displayed algebra bracket. In particular,\n\n$$\\{Q^I_\\alpha,\\bar Q_{\\dot\\beta J}\\}=-2\\sigma^\\mu_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta}P_\\mu\\delta^I{}_J,\\qquad \\{Q^I_\\alpha,Q^J_\\beta\\}=2\\epsilon_{\\alpha\\beta}Z^{IJ},\\qquad \\{\\bar Q_{\\dot\\alpha I},\\bar Q_{\\dot\\beta J}\\}=2\\epsilon_{\\dot\\alpha\\dot\\beta}\\bar Z_{IJ}.$$\n\nThe domain $\\mathcal D$ is invariant under those generators and under $U(\\mathcal P)$. Explicitly, these restrictions define the complex-linear supertranslation representation $\\rho_{\\mathcal D}:\\mathfrak t\\to\\operatorname{End}_{\\mathbb C}(\\mathcal D)$: it sends the abstract $p_\\mu$ to $P_\\mu|_{\\mathcal D}$ and each abstract supercharge or central generator to its named operator restricted to $\\mathcal D$. Invariance of $\\mathcal D$ makes these endomorphisms, and the assumed bracket identities make $\\rho_{\\mathcal D}$ bracket-preserving. In particular, $\\rho_{\\mathcal D}(T_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta})=\\sigma^\\mu_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta}P_\\mu|_{\\mathcal D}$ and $-i\\rho_{\\mathcal D}(ip_\\mu)=P_\\mu|_{\\mathcal D}$. The even group acts on the charge domains exactly: for every $g\\in\\mathrm{SL}(2,\\mathbb C)$, conjugation by $U(g,0)$ sends each closed charge to the corresponding fundamental or dotted spinor transform as an equality of operators, including equality of domains. The central generators transform as Lorentz scalars, commute with translations, and commute on $\\mathcal D$ with all supercharges; these relations also include their domain invariance.\n\nFor every Borel set $B\\subseteq(\\mathbb R^{1,3})^*$ and every charge $Q$ or $Q^*$, require the reducing-projection/domain conditions\n\n$$E(B)D(Q)\\subseteq D(Q),\\qquad Q E(B)\\psi=E(B)Q\\psi\\quad(\\psi\\in D(Q)),$$\n\nand the same conditions with $Q^*$ in place of $Q$. Require also $\\Gamma E(B)=E(B)\\Gamma$ for every Borel $B$. In particular this supplies integrated translation covariance with domain invariance; a relation $[P_\\mu,Q]=0$ on a common core alone is not substituted for it. A closed complex-linear subspace $K$ is graded when $\\Gamma K=K$, equivalently $K=(K\\cap\\mathcal H^+)\\oplus(K\\cap\\mathcal H^-)$. Such a subspace is invariant when $U(g,a)K=K$ for all $(g,a)\\in\\mathcal P$ and each charge and adjoint maps $D(Q)\\cap K$ into $K$, with those intersections dense in $K$. The representation is irreducible when its only such invariant subspaces are $\\{0\\}$ and $\\mathcal H$.",

          "statement": "Use the adopted pure $SU(2)$ Yang–Mills model: $G=SU(2)$, $\\mathfrak g=\\mathfrak{su}(2)$, the selected smooth right-principal bundle sector has no matter fields, and the positive invariant form is $\\kappa(X,Y)=-2\\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$ with $\\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\\delta_{ab}$ for $T_a=-i\\sigma_a/2$, extended bilinearly to the graded coefficient algebra. The gauge condition is a local perturbative choice; it does not assert a global slice or remove all gauge copies. For finite-dimensional regulated data as in the preceding gauge-slice definition, with a smooth right action of a $k$-dimensional Lie group $K$ on $X$, a gauge condition $\\chi:U\\to\\mathbb R^k$, and specified positive densities on $\\mathfrak k$ and $\\mathbb R^k$, the ordinary Faddeev–Popov Jacobian at every $x\\in U$ is the density determinant $\\Delta_{\\rm FP}(x)=|\\det(d\\chi_x\\circ R_x)|$, where $R_x=d(k\\mapsto x\\cdot k)_e$. Let $\\mathcal A_{\\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{g,p}(U)$, $0\\le p\\le4$, be the finite sums of horizontal $p$-forms with coefficients in the ghost-number-$g$ part of this algebra, where the $dx^\\mu$ anticommute under wedge product; set $\\mathcal A_{\\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{g,-1}(U)=\\{0\\}$ and $d_H=dx^\\mu D_\\mu$.\n\nA **formal perturbative renormalization datum** consists of the selected pure SU(2) classical BV action $\\Gamma_0$, the above gauge-fixing choice, the dimensional-regularization prescription $D=4-2\\epsilon$ with a fixed positive reference mass scale $\\mu$, modified minimal subtraction ($\\overline{\\mathrm{MS}}$), and a local counterterm space $\\mathcal C_{\\leq d_*}$. Fix the coupling convention $g_D(\\mu,\\epsilon)=\\mu^\\epsilon g(\\mu)$ and $g_B=\\mu^\\epsilon Z_g g(\\mu)$, where $g(\\mu)$ is dimensionless, $g(\\mu)=g_{\\rm YM}$ at the selected reference scale, and $Z_g=1+O(\\lambda)$ is the formal coupling-renormalization factor. With the geometric connection $A$ of dimension $1$, the dimensionally continued gauge action has coefficient $1/g_D^2=\\mu^{-2\\epsilon}/g(\\mu)^2$; its density has dimension $4-2\\epsilon=D$. The four-dimensional engineering dimensions used for local counterterms below remain those of the $\\epsilon\\to0$ local complex. Use the unrescaled $\\mu$ convention: subtraction removes the pole parts together with the associated $-\\gamma_E+\\log(4\\pi)$ constants, whose one-loop combination is $\\Delta_\\epsilon=1/\\epsilon-\\gamma_E+\\log(4\\pi)$. The definition does not prove the QAP. Define the extended relative local cohomology by\n\n$$H_{\\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{g,p}(s\\mid d_H):=\\frac{\\{a\\in\\mathcal A_{\\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{g,p}(U):\\text{there is }b\\in\\mathcal A_{\\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{g+1,p-1}(U)\\text{ with }sa+d_Hb=0\\}}{\\{sm+d_Hn:m\\in\\mathcal A_{\\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{g-1,p}(U),\\ n\\in\\mathcal A_{\\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{g,p-1}(U)\\}}.$$\n\nFor the counterterm-relevant restriction, let $\\mathcal L_{\\leq d_*}^{g,p}$ be the subspace of $\\mathcal A_{\\mathrm{BV,nm}}^{g,p}(U)$ consisting of Lorentz-covariant local horizontal forms whose coefficient engineering dimension is at most $d_*-4+p$. Here covariance means that under a simultaneous proper orthochronous Lorentz change of coordinates, fields, antifields and jet indices, the expression transforms as a horizontal $p$-form, with no fixed noncovariant background tensor; this is a local covariance requirement on charts and does not require $U$ to be Lorentz invariant. Antifields transform in the dual tensor representations needed to make the displayed master density a scalar. In degree four this says precisely that the density multiplying the oriented volume form is a Lorentz scalar. In degree three it includes the covariant current forms whose horizontal derivative is a scalar density. The four-dimensional weights count $D_\\mu$ as dimension $1$ and $s$ as dimension $0$; they are coefficient weights, so no dimension is assigned to the displayed $dx^\\mu$ for this bound. Put $\\mathcal L^{g,-1}_{\\leq d_*}=0$. The scalar classical master action and the tensorial total derivatives preserve covariance; their dimension rules give $s\\mathcal L^{g,p}_{\\leq d_*}\\subseteq\\mathcal L^{g+1,p}_{\\leq d_*}$ and $d_H\\mathcal L^{g,p}_{\\leq d_*}\\subseteq\\mathcal L^{g,p+1}_{\\leq d_*}$. Define the restricted quotient for $g=0,1$ by\n\n$$H_{\\mathrm{Lor},\\leq d_*}^{g,4}(s\\mid d_H):=\\frac{\\{a\\in\\mathcal L_{\\leq d_*}^{g,4}:sa+d_Hb=0\\text{ for some }b\\in\\mathcal L_{\\leq d_*}^{g+1,3}\\}}{\\{sm+d_Hn:m\\in\\mathcal L_{\\leq d_*}^{g-1,4},\\ n\\in\\mathcal L_{\\leq d_*}^{g,3}\\}}.$$\n\nBoth representatives and equivalence primitives are restricted: $m$ has scalar top-form density of dimension at most $d_*$, and $n$ is a covariant current three-form of coefficient dimension at most $d_*-1$. The regular zero-FI real quotient is the orbit set\n\n$$\\mathcal A^{\\mathrm{reg}}_{k,N}=\\{x:\\mu_{\\mathbb C}(x)=0,\\ \\mu_{\\mathbb R}(x)=0,\\ x\\text{ stable and costable}\\}/U(V).$$\n\nLet $S^4=\\mathbb H\\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and the orientation whose restriction to the stereographic coordinates $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$ on $\\mathbb R^4=S^4\\setminus\\{\\infty\\}$ is $dx^0\\wedge dx^1\\wedge dx^2\\wedge dx^3$. For a smooth right principal $U(N)$-bundle $P\\to S^4$, let $E=P\\times_{U(N)}\\mathbb C^N$ be its Hermitian associated vector bundle, let $A$ be a smooth unitary connection, and let $\\Phi:E|_{\\infty}\\to\\mathbb C^N$ be a unitary framing. For integer $k\\geq0$, the framed ASD sector $\\mathcal M^{\\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ is the set of such framed connections satisfying $F_A^+=0$ and $q_N(P,A)=-k$, modulo smooth unitary gauge transformations whose value at $\\infty$ is the identity in the framing. The finite real line over $z$ has equations $\\mu_1=z_1\\lambda_1-\\bar z_2\\lambda_2$, $\\mu_2=z_2\\lambda_1+\\bar z_1\\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\\lambda_1=\\lambda_2=0$. In the chart $\\lambda_1=1,\\lambda_2=0$, vertical complex orientation followed by the positive orientation of $(z_1,z_2)$ is the complex orientation of $Z$.\n\n\nFor the spinor convention, use the standard spin structure on $S^4$ and $\\operatorname{Spin}(4)\\cong SU(2)_+\\times SU(2)_-$. Let $S^+,S^-$ be the associated rank-two complex spinor bundles, so $T_{\\mathbb C}S^4\\cong S^+\\otimes S^-$. The twistor fibre at $x$ is $\\mathbb P(S_x^+)$, and the complex two-plane associated with $\\ell\\in\\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ is $\\ell\\otimes S_x^-$.           "statement": "Assume AC. Let $V=\\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\\mathbb C^N$, $N\\ge1$, $k\\ge0$, with their standard Hermitian products. For $z=(z_1,z_2)\\in\\mathbb C^2$ put\n\n$$a_z=(B_1-z_1,B_2-z_2,J)^T,\\qquad b_z=(-B_2^\\dagger+\\bar z_2,B_1^\\dagger-\\bar z_1,I^\\dagger)^T,\\qquad D_z=\\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\\dagger\\\\a_z^\\dagger\\end{pmatrix}.$$\n\nThen\n\n$$D_zD_z^\\dagger=\\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\\dagger b_z&\\mu_{\\mathbb C}\\\\\\mu_{\\mathbb C}^\\dagger&a_z^\\dagger a_z\\end{pmatrix},\\qquad b_z^\\dagger b_z-a_z^\\dagger a_z=\\mu_{\\mathbb R}.$$\n\nThe maps $b_z^\\dagger$ are onto for every $z$ exactly when the datum is stable; the maps $a_z$ are injective for every $z$ exactly when it is costable. Consequently, when both moments vanish, regularity is equivalent to $D_z$ being onto for every $z$. On this locus $f_z=a_z^\\dagger a_z=b_z^\\dagger b_z$ is positive definite and\n\n$$P_z=1-D_z^\\dagger\\operatorname{diag}(f_z^{-1},f_z^{-1})D_z$$\n\nis the smooth orthogonal projection onto a rank-$N$ bundle over $\\mathbb R^4$. For regular zero-moment data these maps form a holomorphic bundle monad, trivial on each real line, with middle cohomology on the line over $z$ canonically $\\ker D_z$. Its framing at infinity is $W$. The torus acts on the homogeneous coordinates by $(\\lambda_1,t_1t_2\\lambda_2,t_1\\mu_1,t_2\\mu_2)$ and on the raw data by $(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$; the monad isomorphism has source, middle and target factors $(t_1t_2)^{-1}$, $\\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)$ and $1$, respectively.           "statement": "Let $S^4=\\{X\\in\\mathbb R^5:|X|=1\\}$ have its unit round metric and the orientation which, on the stereographic chart $S^4\\setminus\\{\\infty\\}\\cong\\mathbb R^4$, is $dx_0\\wedge dx_1\\wedge dx_2\\wedge dx_3$. Put $z_1=x_0+ix_1$, $z_2=x_2+ix_3$, and $r^2=|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2$; in these coordinates the metric is $g=4(1+r^2)^{-2}\\sum_{\\mu=0}^3dx_\\mu^2$. Define the Wirtinger derivatives on this chart by\n\n$$\\partial_{z_1}=\\tfrac12(\\partial_{x_0}-i\\partial_{x_1}),\\quad \\partial_{\\bar z_1}=\\tfrac12(\\partial_{x_0}+i\\partial_{x_1}),\\quad \\partial_{z_2}=\\tfrac12(\\partial_{x_2}-i\\partial_{x_3}),\\quad \\partial_{\\bar z_2}=\\tfrac12(\\partial_{x_2}+i\\partial_{x_3});$$\n\nThese vector fields act on the complexification of the real tangent bundle. Fix the antiunitary right quaternionic structure $j:\\mathbb C^4\\to\\mathbb C^4$ in these coordinates by\n\n$$j(\\lambda_1,\\lambda_2,\\mu_1,\\mu_2)=(-\\bar\\lambda_2,\\bar\\lambda_1,-\\bar\\mu_2,\\bar\\mu_1).$$\n\nThus $j$ is conjugate-linear, preserves the standard Hermitian norm, and satisfies $j^2=-I$. Put $\\mathbb H^2=\\mathbb C^4$ with this right quaternionic structure, $Z=\\mathbb CP^3=\\mathbb P_{\\mathbb C}(\\mathbb H^2)$, and define $\\pi:Z\\to\\mathbb HP^1=S^4$ by $\\pi(\\ell)=\\ell+j\\ell$ for each complex line $\\ell\\subset\\mathbb H^2$. Its fibres are projective lines $L_x\\cong\\mathbb CP^1$. In homogeneous coordinates $[\\lambda_1:\\lambda_2:\\mu_1:\\mu_2]$, the fibre over finite $z=(z_1,z_2)$ is the line\n\n$$\\mu_1=z_1\\lambda_1-\\bar z_2\\lambda_2,\\qquad \\mu_2=z_2\\lambda_1+\\bar z_1\\lambda_2,$$\n\nand the fibre over infinity is $L_\\infty=\\{\\lambda_1=\\lambda_2=0\\}$. Give $Z$ the Fubini–Study metric induced by the standard Hermitian metric on $\\mathbb C^4$, and give $\\mathcal O_Z(-1)$, the tautological holomorphic line bundle, its induced Hermitian metric; $\\mathcal O_Z(-2)=\\mathcal O_Z(-1)^{\\otimes2}$ has the tensor-square metric.           "statement": "Use the complex field $\\mathbb C$ with conjugation $z\\mapsto\\overline z$. Fix an integer $N\\ge1$. Let $S=\\mathbb C^2$ have standard basis $s_1,s_2$. For a complex vector space $W$, its conjugate vector space $\\overline W$ consists of symbols $\\overline w$ for $w\\in W$, with addition $\\overline w+\\overline v=\\overline{w+v}$ and scalar action $\\lambda\\overline w=\\overline{\\overline\\lambda w}$. Set $\\dot S=\\overline S$ with dotted basis $\\dot s_{\\dot1}=\\overline{s_1}$ and $\\dot s_{\\dot2}=\\overline{s_2}$. Let $F=\\mathbb C^N$ have standard basis $f_1,\\ldots,f_N$, and let $F^*$ be its complex-linear dual with dual basis $f^1,\\ldots,f^N$ and scalar action $(\\lambda\\ell)(v)=\\lambda\\ell(v)$. Define $\\Lambda^2F=(F\\otimes_{\\mathbb C}F)/\\operatorname{span}_{\\mathbb C}\\{v\\otimes v:v\\in F\\}$; its basis is $f_I\\wedge f_J$ for $1\\le I<J\\le N$, with quotient scalar action. Its conjugate $\\overline{\\Lambda^2F}$ has basis $\\overline{f_I\\wedge f_J}$ and the conjugate scalar action just defined. For $N=1$ these exterior-square spaces are zero. In the displayed bases, $\\mathfrak{sl}(S)=\\{A\\in\\operatorname{End}_{\\mathbb C}(S):\\operatorname{tr}A=0\\}$ and $\\mathfrak{sl}(\\dot S)=\\{B\\in\\operatorname{End}_{\\mathbb C}(\\dot S):\\operatorname{tr}B=0\\}$. Put $\\epsilon_{12}=\\epsilon_{\\dot1\\dot2}=1$ and $\\epsilon_{21}=\\epsilon_{\\dot2\\dot1}=-1$, with zero diagonal. The complex even space is\n\n$$\\mathfrak g_{\\bar0}=\\bigl(\\mathfrak{sl}(S)\\oplus\\mathfrak{sl}(\\dot S)\\bigr)\\oplus V\\oplus C_N,\\qquad V=S\\otimes\\dot S,\\qquad C_N=\\Lambda^2F\\oplus\\overline{\\Lambda^2F}.$$\n\nWrite $T_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta}=s_\\alpha\\otimes\\dot s_{\\dot\\beta}$ for the basis of $V$. The listed central generators form a basis of $C_N$: $Z^{IJ}$ corresponds to $f_I\\wedge f_J$ and $\\bar Z_{IJ}$ to $\\overline{f_I\\wedge f_J}$ for $1\\le I<J\\le N$; extend them by antisymmetry in the flavor indices and set their diagonal entries to zero. The complex odd space is\n\n$$\\mathfrak g_{\\bar1}=(S\\otimes F)\\oplus(\\dot S\\otimes F^*),$$\n\nwith basis $Q^I_\\alpha=s_\\alpha\\otimes f_I$ and $\\bar Q_{\\dot\\alpha I}=\\dot s_{\\dot\\alpha}\\otimes f^I$. A homogeneous vector has parity $|x|\\in\\{0,1\\}$. The bracket is complex-bilinear, preserves parity, and obeys $[x,y]=-(-1)^{|x||y|}[y,x]$.           "statement": "Fix an integer $d\geq2$, a closed compact oriented smooth $d$-manifold $M$, and a finite ordered triangulation $K$ of $M$, meaning a finite vertex-ordered simplicial complex whose geometric realization is $M$. The model specifies its **tangential structure** as follows. Write $BO(d)=\operatorname{Gr}_d(\mathbb R^\infty)$ for the space of $d$-dimensional linear subspaces of $\mathbb R^\infty=\bigcup_N\mathbb R^N$, with the direct-limit topology, and $\gamma_d\to BO(d)$ for the vector bundle whose fiber at a plane is that plane. Fix a continuous map $\tau_M:M\to BO(d)$ and a vector-bundle isomorphism $TM\cong\tau_M^*\gamma_d$. Fix a topological space $X$ and a continuous map $\xi:X\to BO(d)$ with the homotopy lifting property: for every topological space $Y$, continuous $u:Y\to X$ and continuous $H:Y\times[0,1]\to BO(d)$ satisfying $H(y,0)=\xi(u(y))$, there is a continuous $\widetilde H:Y\times[0,1]\to X$ with $\widetilde H(y,0)=u(y)$ and $\xi\circ\widetilde H=H$. Such a map is called a fibration here. Specify a continuous lift $\theta:M\to X$ satisfying $\xi\circ\theta=\tau_M$, and an orientation of $\theta^*\xi^*\gamma_d$ inducing the chosen orientation of $TM$. Pullback here gives the bundle with fiber $(\gamma_d)_{\xi(\theta(m))}$ at $m\in M$. These maps, bundle identification and orientation are specified data and remain fixed under the internal background gauge arrows below; the existence of a lift is an admissibility condition, not asserted for arbitrary $M$ and $\xi$. For orientation alone, one may take $X$ to be the space of oriented $d$-planes and $\xi$ the map forgetting their orientations; additional lifting requirements must instead be encoded by the specified $X$, $\xi$ and $\theta$. A **selected finite-regulator Euclidean model** on $K$ specifies its exact symmetry groups, field representations, finite field-value sets $X_\sigma$ for cells $\sigma\in K$, constraints, and configuration spaces $\Phi_x\subseteq\prod_{\sigma\in K}X_\sigma$ for each background $x$. It also specifies a dimensionless Euclidean action $S_x:\Phi_x\to\mathbb R$, finite measure weights $\mu_x:\Phi_x\to\mathbb C$, and a unital complex subalgebra $\mathcal O_x\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Phi_x,\mathbb C)$ of model-defined observables. For a subcomplex $L\subseteq K$, write $\mathcal O_x(L)$ for the subalgebra of functions depending only on field variables on $L$; an observable is **local** if it belongs to $\mathcal O_x(L)$ for some specified $L$. A line observable has support on a one-dimensional subcomplex. Write $W_x(\phi):=\mu_x(\phi)e^{-S_x(\phi)}$. For local insertion functions $o_{j,x}:\Phi_x\to\mathbb C$, define the unnormalized correlator by $C_x(O_1,\ldots,O_n):=\sum_{\phi\in\Phi_x}W_x(\phi)\prod_{j=1}^n o_{j,x}(\phi)$; the empty tuple has value $Z_x=C_x()$. Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$; cochain labels, action phases, and the partition weight are dimensionless. The model separately assigns dimensions to any continuous field quantities or observables it includes. No continuum limit or Lorentzian continuation is part of this definition.

The ordinary-observable sum above is the no-defect sector of the model's **complete insertion functional**. For each background $x$, the model declares a set $\mathcal I_x$ of admissible inputs $I=(b;D;X_1,\ldots,X_n)$: $b$ specifies all remaining geometric and boundary data (there is no physical boundary for the closed $M$ here); $D$ is a finite decorated defect network; and each $X_j$ is a typed local, line, or other model-admitted insertion, possibly another decorated network. A network has finitely many smooth locally closed strata whose closures obey the frontier condition, the complete incidence relation, and model-specified field, orientation, coorientation, framing, and ordered junction data on each stratum, as in the topological-defect definition. The model states all disjointness, incidence, and label admissibility conditions. For every $I\in\mathcal I_x$ it supplies a finite set $\Omega_x(I)$ of field configurations, including any defect or junction variables and modified constraints, and a complex weight $w_x(I;\omega)$ with its declared normalization. Its unnormalized complete correlator is

$$
\widehat C_x(I):=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega_x(I)}w_x(I;\omega)\in\mathbb C.
$$

For no defect and a tuple of ordinary local insertions this must reduce to $\Omega_x(I)=\Phi_x$ and $w_x(I;\phi)=W_x(\phi)\prod_j o_{j,x}(\phi)$, so $\widehat C_x(I)=C_x(O_1,\ldots,O_n)$. The empty network, empty insertion tuple has value $Z_x$. This is conditional finite model data, not a construction of defect correlators from the ordinary observable algebra or from the 2-group labels.

The regulator includes a precise support-move convention. Defect supports at the displayed regulator inputs are represented by subcomplexes, with their smooth strata and decorations specified. A permitted decorated isotopy preserves strata, incidence and ordered junctions, transports every label and framing, fixes $b$ and the background, and avoids all other insertions. A claim of topologicality along such a smooth path requires the model to supply complete correlators at every intermediate support and comparisons with the endpoint regulator inputs; if subdivisions or other regulator presentations are used, their field sums and comparison maps must be supplied. The model must verify equality of the complete correlators under these comparisons. At a fixed triangulation the same requirement applies to each declared discrete support move, with its exact transport of complete inputs. A path through supports not represented by subcomplexes is not evaluated merely by writing the fixed-$K$ ordinary sum. These extra assignments do not assert a continuum limit or triangulation independence.

Let $G$ be the selected finite discrete internal $0$-form symmetry group. Its action on the model's local field and observable data is specified by group homomorphisms into the corresponding automorphism groups. Let $A$ be the selected finite discrete abelian $1$-form symmetry group, written additively, with the exact support, charge, and background conventions of the selected p-form symmetry model. The Abelian group $A$ is the ordinary local invertible $1$-form branch of the p-form definition. The $0$-form group $G$ may be non-Abelian, and its action on $A$ and the Postnikov data below retain the mixed 2-group structure; this does not replace $A$ by a non-Abelian local $1$-form label group. The group is effective in the selected model: elements inducing identical actions in every admitted correlator, observable, and background are identified. Each generator $U_a(\Sigma)$ is a defect insertion with support $j(\Sigma)$, where $\Sigma$ is a smooth manifold without boundary and $j:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$ is a smooth embedding with closed codimension-two image represented by a subcomplex of $K$; the insertion includes the model-specified local field or operator data and any required orientation, coorientation, framing, or junction data on that image. It is topological when $\widehat C_x$ is invariant for every complete admissible input under the permitted decorated support isotopies and regulator comparisons just specified, avoiding all other insertions. The generators fuse by $U_aU_{a'}=U_{a+a'}$. Following the selected p-form symmetry model, a **genuine line observable** is supported on a closed embedded one-dimensional submanifold, represented here by a one-dimensional subcomplex of $K$, and is defined without an attached higher-dimensional support; the model specifies its crossing junction and action. If, for a nonzero genuine line observable $O_\gamma$, the crossing maps restrict to a complex-linear representation $R:A\to\operatorname{GL}(\mathbb C O_\gamma)$, write $R_a(O_\gamma)=\chi_\gamma(a)O_\gamma$. Then $\chi_\gamma:A\to\mathbb C^\times$ is a homomorphism. Since $A$ is finite, every $a\in A$ has finite order $m$, so $\chi_\gamma(a)^m=\chi_\gamma(0)=1$ and $|\chi_\gamma(a)|=1$. Thus $\chi_\gamma$ is a character in $\widehat A:=\operatorname{Hom}(A,U(1))$; it is continuous because $A$ is finite and discrete. Sweeping $U_a(\Sigma)$ once across the line in the chosen positive orientation multiplies the correlator by $\chi_\gamma(a)$. Other line observables need not carry a scalar character. The selected $0$-form symmetry acts on these defect labels through a specified left action $\rho:G\to\operatorname{Aut}(A)$.

Here the representation condition means $R_{a+a'}=R_aR_{a'}$ and $R_0=\operatorname{id}$; $\mathbb C^\times=\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$ and $U(1)=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$. The unit-modulus conclusion uses finiteness of $A$ and this representation law, not a Hilbert-space inner product.

Choose a normalized inhomogeneous $3$-cocycle $\beta:G^3\to A$ for this left action; normalized means it vanishes if any argument is the identity, and the cocycle equation is

$$
\rho_g\beta(h,k,l)-\beta(gh,k,l)+\beta(g,hk,l)-\beta(g,h,kl)+\beta(g,h,k)=0.
$$

For a normalized $2$-cochain $c:G^2\to A$, set

$$
(\delta_\rho c)(g,h,k):=\rho_g c(h,k)-c(gh,k)+c(g,hk)-c(g,h).
$$

Two normalized $3$-cocycles represent the same Postnikov class when their difference is $\delta_\rho c$ for such a normalized $c$; $[\beta]$ denotes this equivalence class. The skeletal associator convention is directed from $(gh)k$ to $g(hk)$. A discrete background is nondynamical model data and is not summed over. It is an object $x=(a,B)$ of the finite background gauge $2$-groupoid on $K$: $a_{ij}\in G$ is a flat edge cochain, $a_{ij}a_{jk}=a_{ik}$ on every ordered triangle; $B_{ijk}\in A$ is a face cochain at its first vertex; and on every ordered tetrahedron

$$
(\delta_a B)_{ijkl}:=\rho_{a_{ij}}B_{jkl}-B_{ikl}+B_{ijl}-B_{ijk}=\beta(a_{ij},a_{jk},a_{kl})=(a^*\beta)_{ijkl}.
$$

Thus the two background fields are constrained and are not independent. A $1$-gauge arrow is given by vertex labels $g_i\in G$ and edge labels $\lambda_{ij}\in A$, with

$$
a'_{ij}=g_i a_{ij}g_j^{-1},\qquad \zeta^g_{ijk}=-\beta(g_i,a_{ij},a_{jk})+\beta(a'_{ij},g_j,a_{jk})-\beta(a'_{ij},a'_{jk},g_k),
$$

$$
B'_{ijk}=\rho_{g_i}B_{ijk}+\zeta^g_{ijk}+\rho_{a'_{ij}}\lambda_{jk}-\lambda_{ik}+\lambda_{ij}.
$$

A $2$-arrow between $1$-arrows with the same vertex labels $g$ and edge labels $\lambda,\lambda'$ is a vertex $A$-cochain $t$ satisfying $\lambda'-\lambda=\delta_{a'}t$, where $(\delta_{a'}t)_{ij}=\rho_{a'_{ij}}t_j-t_i$; vertical composition adds these cochains. For consecutive $1$-arrows $(g,\lambda)$ then $(h,\mu)$, their composite has vertex labels $hg$ and edge labels $\nu_{ij}=\rho_{h_i}\lambda_{ij}+\mu_{ij}+\tau_{ij}$, where $\tau_{ij}=\beta(h_i,g_i,a_{ij})-\beta(h_i,a'_{ij},g_j)+\beta(a''_{ij},h_j,g_j)$ and $a''_{ij}=h_i a'_{ij}h_j^{-1}$. Horizontal composition sends $2$-arrow cochains $t,s$ to $s+\rho_h t$. For three consecutive arrows with vertex labels $g,h,k$, the associator is the vertex cochain $\sigma_i=\beta(k_i,h_i,g_i)$; identity arrows have vertex labels $e$ and edge labels $0$, and unit constraints are identity $2$-arrows. The pentagon and triangle coherence equations are those of this finite background gauge $2$-groupoid.

A **finite model fiber** is a tuple $D_x=(\Phi_x,\mathcal O_x,W_x,\{\mathcal O_x(L)\}_{L\subseteq K})$ as specified above. Let $\mathfrak M$ be the strict $2$-category whose objects are these fibers. A $1$-morphism $F=(T,\alpha):D_x\to D_y$ consists of a bijection $T:\Phi_x\to\Phi_y$ and a unital complex-algebra isomorphism $\alpha:\mathcal O_x\to\mathcal O_y$ such that $(\alpha O)(T\phi)=O(\phi)$ for all $O\in\mathcal O_x$ and $\phi\in\Phi_x$, and such that $\alpha$ preserves the declared local subalgebras. It must also transport weights by a configuration-independent nonzero scalar: there exists $c_F\in\mathbb C^\times$ with $W_y(T\phi)=c_FW_x(\phi)$ for every $\phi\in\Phi_x$. The scalar is not additional morphism data; it is unique when $W_x$ is not identically zero, while no uniqueness is asserted for zero-weight or empty fibers. The phase-law case requires a model-specified choice in $U(1)$, with the coherence stipulated below. Composition is $(S,\gamma)\circ(T,\alpha)=(S\circ T,\gamma\circ\alpha)$ and the identity is $(\operatorname{id}_{\Phi_x},\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal O_x})$. A $2$-morphism $(J,j):(T,\alpha)\Rightarrow(T',\alpha')$ has target-fiber data $J:\Phi_y\to\Phi_y$ a bijection and $j:\mathcal O_y\to\mathcal O_y$ a unital complex-algebra automorphism, with $T'=J\circ T$, $\alpha'=j\circ\alpha$, $j(O)=O\circ J^{-1}$ for every $O\in\mathcal O_y$, $j$ preserving the declared local subalgebras, and $W_y(J\psi)=W_y(\psi)$ for every $\psi\in\Phi_y$. Identity $2$-morphisms are identity pairs; vertical composition is $(J',j')\circ(J,j)=(J'\circ J,j'\circ j)$. If $(J,j):F\Rightarrow F'$ and $(Q,q):H\Rightarrow H'$ with $F=(T,\alpha):D_x\to D_y$ and $H=(S,\gamma):D_y\to D_z$, their horizontal composite is $(Q\circ S\circ J\circ S^{-1},\ q\circ\gamma\circ j\circ\gamma^{-1}):H\circ F\Rightarrow H'\circ F'$. These formulas define the target's identity and composition laws.

In the target $2$-category, locality preservation means $\alpha(\mathcal O_x(L))=\mathcal O_y(L)$ for each subcomplex $L\subseteq K$, and $j(\mathcal O_y(L))=\mathcal O_y(L)$ for each target-side $2$-morphism. Every $2$-morphism compares $1$-morphisms with the same source and target fibers. The identity $1$-morphism has scalar $1$, a composite $H\circ F$ has an admissible scalar $c_Hc_F$, and the inverse pair $(T^{-1},\alpha^{-1})$ has scalar $c_F^{-1}$. Thus $1$-morphisms are closed under these operations, including when some configuration weights vanish. Vertical composites and inverses of $2$-morphisms preserve the target weight and local algebras.

For horizontal closure, put $\psi=S\xi\in\Phi_z$. Since $W_z(S\xi)=c_HW_y(\xi)$ and $J$ preserves $W_y$, one has $W_z(SJS^{-1}\psi)=c_HW_y(J\xi)=c_HW_y(\xi)=W_z(\psi)$. Composing with $Q$ still preserves $W_z$. The algebra component is pullback by the inverse of the resulting configuration bijection and preserves each local subalgebra, because $q$, $\gamma$, $j$, and their inverses do so. Its source and target are correct since $(QSJS^{-1})(ST)=QSJT=S'T'$ and $(q\gamma j\gamma^{-1})(\gamma\alpha)=q\gamma j\alpha=\gamma'\alpha'$. Here $S'=QS$, $T'=JT$, $\gamma'=q\gamma$, and $\alpha'=j\alpha$.

Finally, for fixed parallel $1$-morphisms $(T,\alpha)$ and $(T',\alpha')$, any $2$-morphism is uniquely forced to have $J=T'T^{-1}$ and $j=\alpha'\alpha^{-1}$; it exists precisely when this pair meets the stated conditions. Consequently the hom categories have at most one arrow between any two objects. The displayed $1$-composition is strictly associative and unital. Every iterated horizontal composition, horizontal identity law, and either side of the interchange equation is now a well-typed $2$-morphism with the same source and target as its counterpart, so uniqueness proves the required equalities. This verifies that $\mathfrak M$ is a strict $2$-category.

A **finite 2-group background coupling** is a pseudofunctor $F:\mathcal B(K)\to\mathfrak M$, where $\mathcal B(K)$ denotes the finite background gauge $2$-groupoid on $K$ defined above. Explicitly, it assigns a model fiber $D_x$ to each background object, a $1$-morphism $(T_f,\alpha_f)$ to each $1$-arrow, and a target-fiber $2$-morphism $(J_\eta,j_\eta)$ to each $2$-arrow $\eta:f\Rightarrow f'$. It preserves identity $2$-arrows and vertical composition. It also supplies invertible comparison $2$-morphisms $\kappa_{g,f}:F(g)\circ F(f)\Rightarrow F(g\circ f)$ and unit $2$-morphisms $\iota_x:\operatorname{id}_{D_x}\Rightarrow F(\operatorname{id}_x)$. For composable $2$-arrows $\eta:f\Rightarrow f'$ and $\theta:g\Rightarrow g'$, horizontal naturality requires

$$
F(\theta\ast\eta)\circ\kappa_{g,f}=\kappa_{g',f'}\circ(F(\theta)\ast F(\eta)).
$$

For the background associator $a_{h,g,f}: (h\circ g)\circ f\Rightarrow h\circ(g\circ f)$, the comparison maps obey

$$
F(a_{h,g,f})\circ\kappa_{h\circ g,f}\circ(\kappa_{h,g}\ast\operatorname{id}_{F(f)})=\kappa_{h,g\circ f}\circ(\operatorname{id}_{F(h)}\ast\kappa_{g,f}).
$$

For the left and right unitors $\ell_f:\operatorname{id}_y\circ f\Rightarrow f$ and $r_f:f\circ\operatorname{id}_x\Rightarrow f$, they obey

$$
F(\ell_f)\circ\kappa_{\operatorname{id}_y,f}\circ(\iota_y\ast\operatorname{id}_{F(f)})=\operatorname{id}_{F(f)},\qquad F(r_f)\circ\kappa_{f,\operatorname{id}_x}\circ(\operatorname{id}_{F(f)}\ast\iota_x)=\operatorname{id}_{F(f)}.
$$

The coupling also specifies a bijective transport $f_*:\mathcal I_x\to\mathcal I_y$ of complete admissible inputs along each gauge arrow $f:x\to y$, including its action on $b$, all support decorations, and junctions, together with a bijection $\widetilde T_{f,I}:\Omega_x(I)\to\Omega_y(f_*I)$. On the ordinary sector these reduce to the specified observable transport and $T_f$. For a $2$-arrow $\eta:f\Rightarrow f'$, the model supplies a bijection of target input data sending $f_*I$ to $f'_*I$ and a configuration bijection $\widetilde J_{\eta,I}:\Omega_y(f_*I)\to\Omega_y(f'_*I)$ with $\widetilde T_{f',I}=\widetilde J_{\eta,I}\widetilde T_{f,I}$ and preservation of the complete integrand. Comparison maps similarly run from $g_*(f_*I)$ to $(g\circ f)_*I$, with configuration maps from $\Omega_z(g_*f_*I)$ to $\Omega_z((g\circ f)_*I)$; unit maps run from $I$ to $(\operatorname{id}_x)_*I$. On each such fiber these maps obey the identity, vertical, horizontal, associator and unit equations displayed above, using their stated source and target inputs, and they intertwine every declared support move. Their weight transformation law is additional model data. In the coherent phase-law setting on complete inputs the model must in particular verify

$$
w_y(f_*I;\widetilde T_{f,I}\omega)=\chi_f(x)w_x(I;\omega)
$$

for every admitted $I$ and $\omega$, with the same configuration-independent phase and identity, composition and $2$-isomorphism conditions as below. This implies $\widehat C_y(f_*I)=\chi_f(x)\widehat C_x(I)$ by finite reindexing; ordinary-sector covariance alone does not establish this extension. Likewise, every claimed internal symmetry action on observables and defects includes a bijection on the complete typed insertion and combined background/boundary data, preserving admissibility and the complete correlator after that simultaneous transport; a specified anomalous background gauge transformation instead has its stated phase law. Crossing actions and their junctions must be defined on these complete inputs before a defect-charge relation is asserted.

Here $\ast$ denotes horizontal composition or whiskering of $2$-morphisms. These equations give the precise identity, vertical, horizontal, associator, and unit coherence required of the model assignment. The action and measure are model inputs; the finite 2-group data alone do not choose them or determine their transformation phase.

A permitted background counterterm is a model-declared dimensionless functional $L_x\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$ that is a finite sum of functions, each depending only on cochain labels in one simplex or a specified finite cluster of simplices; it reweights the model by $e^{iL_x}$. If under a gauge arrow $f:x\to y$ all unnormalized correlators transform by a common phase $\chi_f(x)\in U(1)$, coherence requires $\chi_{\mathrm{id}_x}(x)=1$, $\chi_{g\circ f}(x)=\chi_g(y)\chi_f(x)$ for composable arrows, and equal phases for $2$-isomorphic arrows. The residual background anomaly is the class of these phases under $\chi_f(x)\mapsto e^{iL_y}\chi_f(x)e^{-iL_x}$ for the permitted counterterms. The anomaly is absent in the selected scheme exactly when an allowed counterterm makes every such phase $1$. The Postnikov class specifies the background constraint and gauge transformations; it is not itself the model's transformation phase or anomaly.           "statement": "Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Fix $r>0$ with units of length and the round oriented sphere
$$\mathbb S^3_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^4:\textstyle\sum_{\alpha=1}^4 y_\alpha^2=r^2\}$$
with its induced Riemannian metric, no boundary, and its unique spin structure: $\mathbb S^3$ is spin, and its spin structures form a torsor for $H^1(\mathbb S^3;\mathbb Z_2)=0$. Here three-dimensional $\mathcal N=m$ counts $m$ independent two-component real (Majorana) supersymmetry generators before Euclidean continuation; their Euclidean spinor parameters are complex. Superconformal means the algebra also contains conformal transformations and the corresponding special-superconformal supersymmetry generators. Adopt the source-specific ABJM model on this background, viewed through one chosen three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ subalgebra. Its gauge group is $G=U(N)\times U(N)$ with $N\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}$ and supersymmetric Chern–Simons levels $k$ and $-k$, where $k\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$. The global group includes both central $U(1)$ factors. Write $\operatorname{tr}_N$ for the trace in the defining representation of either factor; in the Kapustin–Willett–Yaakov convention the level multiplies $\operatorname{tr}_N/(4\pi)$ in the supersymmetric Chern–Simons action.

Write $M=\mathbb S^3_r$ and $g$ for its metric. A spin structure here is a principal $\operatorname{Spin}(3)$ bundle $P\to M$ with a two-to-one equivariant map to the bundle of oriented $g$-orthonormal tangent frames, covering the double covering $\operatorname{Spin}(3)\cong SU(2)\to SO(3)$. Let $\rho:SU(2)\to U(\mathbb C^2)$ be the defining representation and $S=P\times_\rho\mathbb C^2$ its complex rank-two spinor bundle. The fiber Hermitian metric is induced by $h(v,w)=v^\dagger w$ on $\mathbb C^2$. The connection $\nabla^S:C^\infty(M,S)\to C^\infty(M,T^*M\otimes S)$ is induced by the Levi-Civita connection. In a local oriented orthonormal coframe $e^a$, with dual frame $E_a$, choose
$$\gamma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad\gamma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad\gamma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$
Thus $\gamma_a^\dagger=\gamma_a$, $\gamma_a\gamma_b+\gamma_b\gamma_a=2\delta_{ab}I_2$, and $\gamma_a\gamma_b=\delta_{ab}I_2+i\epsilon_{abc}\gamma_c$, with $\epsilon_{123}=1$. Clifford multiplication by a real one-form $\eta$ is $\gamma(\eta)=\sum_a\eta(E_a)\gamma_a$; in coordinates $\gamma_\mu=e^a_\mu\gamma_a$ and $\gamma^\mu=g^{\mu\nu}\gamma_\nu$. If $\omega_{ab}$ are the Levi-Civita connection one-forms, then $\nabla^S=d+\tfrac14\omega_{ab}\gamma_a\gamma_b$ in a spin frame. Coordinate indices in the formulas below are contracted with $g$; orthonormal indices with $\delta_{ab}$.

For a gauge representation $R$, let $E_R=M\times R$ be its associated bundle on the stated trivial gauge bundle. Spinor fields are smooth sections of $S\otimes E_R$; vector gauginos use the complexified adjoint representation and chiral spinors the indicated bifundamental representation. Fermionic components have odd coefficients in a complex Grassmann algebra (an algebra generated by anticommuting odd variables). Barred fermions are independent sections of the corresponding dual bundle; the dagger on fermions in the displayed actions denotes this independent dual variable, whereas on ordinary commuting spinors it denotes the Hermitian dual. Spinor covariant derivatives use the tensor product of $\nabla^S$ and the specified gauge connection. The $SU(2)$-invariant alternating form is $C=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$; its dual map is $v\mapsto v^T C$, with $T$ the ordinary matrix transpose. Contractions of two column spinors use this form. Scalar and auxiliary components are smooth sections of $E_R$, with even coefficients. These conventions type the actions and variations below; all fields are complexified when acted on by the selected odd supersymmetry derivation.

Each $\mathcal N=2$ vector multiplet has a Hermitian matrix-valued connection $A_\mu$ (or $\widehat A_\mu$), a real Hermitian adjoint scalar $\sigma$ (or $\widehat\sigma$), a two-component complex gaugino $\lambda$ (or $\widehat\lambda$), and a real auxiliary scalar $D$ (or $\widehat D$). In an oriented coordinate chart the first factor's source-normalized action is
$$S_{\mathrm{CS},k}=\frac{k}{4\pi}\int d^3x\,\operatorname{tr}_N\!\left(\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho}\left(A_\mu\partial_\nu A_\rho+\frac{2i}{3}A_\mu A_\nu A_\rho\right)+\sqrt g\left(-\lambda^\dagger\lambda+2D\sigma\right)\right);$$
the second factor uses the same expression with $(A,\lambda,D,\sigma,k)$ replaced by $(\widehat A,\widehat\lambda,\widehat D,\widehat\sigma,-k)$. Here $\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho}$ is the oriented Levi-Civita density. Write $A=A_\mu dx^\mu$ and $\widehat A=\widehat A_\mu dx^\mu$ for the Hermitian connection one-forms, with curvatures $F_A=dA+iA\wedge A$ and $F_{\widehat A}=d\widehat A+i\widehat A\wedge\widehat A$. For smooth gauge transformations $U,\widehat U:\mathbb S^3_r\to U(N)$, use
$$A\mapsto UAU^{-1}+i\,dU\,U^{-1},\qquad \widehat A\mapsto\widehat U\widehat A\widehat U^{-1}+i\,d\widehat U\,\widehat U^{-1}.$$
This convention makes $d+iA$ covariant on a fundamental column and makes each curvature transform by conjugation. In components, $F_{A,\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu+i[A_\mu,A_\nu]$. An adjoint field $X$ transforms as $X\mapsto UXU^{-1}$ and has covariant derivative $D_\mu X=\nabla_\mu X+i[A_\mu,X]$; use the hatted connection for the second adjoint factor. Spinor covariant derivatives also contain the Levi-Civita spin connection.

The matter consists of two chiral multiplets $A_a$, $a=1,2$, in $(\mathbf N,\overline{\mathbf N})$ and two $B_{\dot a}$, $\dot a=1,2$, in $(\overline{\mathbf N},\mathbf N)$. A chiral multiplet means a complex scalar, a two-component complex spinor, and a complex auxiliary scalar in its stated representation. For $(U,\widehat U)\in G$, the transformations are $A_a\mapsto U A_a\widehat U^{-1}$ and $B_{\dot a}\mapsto\widehat U B_{\dot a}U^{-1}$; the corresponding rules hold for their spinor and auxiliary components. The covariant derivatives on scalars are
$$D_\mu A_a=\partial_\mu A_a+iA_\mu A_a-iA_a\widehat A_\mu,\qquad D_\mu B_{\dot a}=\partial_\mu B_{\dot a}+i\widehat A_\mu B_{\dot a}-iB_{\dot a}A_\mu.$$
Spinors also carry the Levi-Civita spin connection. The vector-multiplet fields act on a bifundamental by left multiplication from its fundamental factor minus right multiplication from its antifundamental factor; in particular $\sigma\cdot A_a=\sigma A_a-A_a\widehat\sigma$.

The round-sphere component action for one chiral multiplet $(\phi,\psi,F)$ of $R$-charge $\Delta=\tfrac12$, in the representation determined by its bifundamental type, is
$$S_{\mathrm{chiral}}=\int_{\mathbb S^3_r}d^3x\,\sqrt g\left((D_\mu\phi)^\dagger D^\mu\phi+\frac{3}{4r^2}\phi^\dagger\phi+i\psi^\dagger\gamma^\mu D_\mu\psi+F^\dagger F-\phi^\dagger\sigma^2\phi+\phi^\dagger D\phi-\psi^\dagger\sigma\psi+i\phi^\dagger\lambda^\dagger\psi-i\psi^\dagger\lambda\phi\right).$$
The representation-valued $\sigma,D,\lambda$ in this expression act by the first-factor action minus the second-factor action. Sum this action over the four chiral multiplets.

The adopted $\mathcal N=2$ superpotential is
$$W=\frac{2\pi}{k}\epsilon^{ab}\epsilon^{\dot a\dot b}\operatorname{tr}_N(A_aB_{\dot a}A_bB_{\dot b})=\frac{4\pi}{k}\operatorname{tr}_N(A_1B_1A_2B_2-A_1B_2A_2B_1),$$
where $\epsilon^{12}=1=-\epsilon^{21}$ and all other components vanish. Let $\phi^I$ range over all complex matrix entries of the four chiral scalars, and set $W_I=\partial W/\partial\phi^I$ and $W_{IJ}=\partial_I\partial_JW$. Let spinor indices $\rho,\tau$ range over $\{1,2\}$ and set $\varepsilon^{12}=1=-\varepsilon^{21}$ with all other components zero. The adopted off-shell component interaction is
$$S_W=\int_{\mathbb S^3_r}d^3x\,\sqrt g\left( \sum_I F^I W_I-\frac12\sum_{I,J}\varepsilon^{\rho\tau}\psi^I_\rho\psi^J_\tau W_{IJ} +\sum_I \bar F_I\overline{W_I} -\frac12\sum_{I,J}\varepsilon^{\rho\tau}\bar\psi^I_\rho\bar\psi^J_\tau\overline{W_{IJ}} \right).$$
Here the barred polynomial has conjugate coefficients and barred field labels; the paired auxiliary variables lie on the chosen conjugate contour, while barred Euclidean fermions are independent Grassmann variables. The displayed $F$-terms are not integrated out. The superpotential is the holomorphic interaction that supplies the chiral auxiliary-field and Yukawa terms. This is the ABJM quartic interaction; the adopted quantum model has the enhanced $\mathcal N=6$ superconformal symmetry, while localization uses only the selected $\mathcal N=2$ subalgebra. For $\theta\in\mathbb R/(4\pi\mathbb Z)$, the compact $R$-symmetry circle action on a chiral multiplet of charge $\Delta$ is $(\phi,\psi,F)\mapsto(e^{i\Delta\theta}\phi,e^{i(\Delta-1)\theta}\psi,e^{i(\Delta-2)\theta}F)$. The superconformal dimension is the weight under dilatations; in this model the scalar weight and scalar $R$-charge are $\Delta=\tfrac12$, the fermion and auxiliary scaling dimensions are $\Delta+\tfrac12=1$ and $\Delta+1=\tfrac32$, and their $R$-charges are $\Delta-1$ and $\Delta-2$, respectively. The $4\pi$ period makes the half-integer charges single-valued; equivalently one may use a $2\pi$-periodic angle $\vartheta=\theta/2$ and integer charges $(1,-1,-3)$. Set all real masses and Fayet–Iliopoulos parameters to zero. A real mass here is the constant scalar in a background flavor vector multiplet; a Fayet–Iliopoulos parameter is the coefficient of the auxiliary $D$ field for an abelian vector multiplet. The level $k$ is dimensionless and $r$ has units of length; $[A_\mu]=[\sigma]=r^{-1}$, $[\lambda]=r^{-3/2}$, $[D]=r^{-2}$, $[\phi]=r^{-1/2}$, $[\psi]=r^{-1}$, and $[F]=r^{-3/2}$. These dimensions make every displayed action density have units $r^{-3}$.

The smooth field domain consists of pairs of smooth connections and the listed smooth associated matter and auxiliary fields on the trivial $U(N)\times U(N)$ bundles. The smooth gauge group is $\mathcal G=C^\infty(\mathbb S^3_r,U(N)\times U(N))$, acting by the transformations above. For infinitesimal Hermitian parameters $\alpha,\widehat\alpha$ with $(U,\widehat U)=(e^{-i\alpha},e^{-i\widehat\alpha})$ at first order, write $D_A\alpha=d\alpha+i[A,\alpha]$ and $D_{\widehat A}\widehat\alpha=d\widehat\alpha+i[\widehat A,\widehat\alpha]$; then $\delta A=D_A\alpha$ and $\delta\widehat A=D_{\widehat A}\widehat\alpha$. The Lorenz gauge-fixing function is
$$\mathcal F(A,\widehat A)=(\nabla^\mu A_\mu,\nabla^\mu\widehat A_\mu),$$
Here $\nabla$ is the Levi-Civita derivative on the one-form index, applied componentwise to the Lie-algebra values.
and its derivative along a gauge orbit is the Faddeev–Popov operator
$$\mathcal M_{A,\widehat A}(\alpha,\widehat\alpha) =(\nabla^\mu D_{A,\mu}\alpha,\nabla^\mu D_{\widehat A,\mu}\widehat\alpha).$$
Let $c,\widehat c$ be odd Lie-algebra-valued ghost scalars, $\bar c,\bar{\widehat c}$ odd antighosts, and $b,\widehat b$ even multiplier scalars; set $[c]=[\widehat c]=r^0$ and $[\bar c]=[b]=[\bar{\widehat c}]=[\widehat b]=r^{-1}$, and in the Lorenz limit take $b=i\beta$, $\widehat b=i\widehat\beta$ with real $\beta,\widehat\beta$. The Faddeev–Popov differential $s$ is the odd derivation
$$sA=D_Ac,\quad s\widehat A=D_{\widehat A}\widehat c,\quad sc=-\frac{i}{2}[c,c]_{\rm gr},\quad s\widehat c=-\frac{i}{2}[\widehat c,\widehat c]_{\rm gr},\quad s\bar c=b,\quad s\bar{\widehat c}=\widehat b,\quad sb=s\widehat b=0,$$
where $[X,Y]_{\rm gr}=XY-(-1)^{|X||Y|}YX$ is the parity-graded matrix bracket; its Jacobi identity gives $s^2=0$. On every other field $s$ is the infinitesimal gauge action with $\alpha,\widehat\alpha$ replaced by $c,\widehat c$; in particular $sA_a=-icA_a+iA_a\widehat c$ and $sB_{\dot a}=-i\widehat cB_{\dot a}+iB_{\dot a}c$. The gauge-fixing fermion and its conventional BRST part are
$$\Psi_{\rm gf}=\int_{\mathbb S^3_r}d^3x\,\sqrt g\,\operatorname{tr}_N\left(\bar c\,\nabla^\mu A_\mu+\frac{\xi}{2r}\bar c\,b+\bar{\widehat c}\,\nabla^\mu\widehat A_\mu+\frac{\xi}{2r}\bar{\widehat c}\,\widehat b\right),\qquad s\Psi_{\rm gf}=\int_{\mathbb S^3_r}d^3x\,\sqrt g\,\operatorname{tr}_N\left(b\,\nabla^\mu A_\mu+\widehat b\,\nabla^\mu\widehat A_\mu+\frac{\xi}{2r}(b^2+\widehat b^2)-\bar c\,\nabla^\mu D_{A,\mu}c-\bar{\widehat c}\,\nabla^\mu D_{\widehat A,\mu}\widehat c\right).$$
Here $\xi\geq0$ is a dimensionless gauge parameter; the source uses its Lorenz limit $\xi\to0$, taken before the multiplier integral. With $b=i\beta$ and $\widehat b=i\widehat\beta$, integration over the real multiplier fields $\beta,\widehat\beta$ gives the Fourier representations of the two Lorenz delta functionals. These conditions define a local gauge slice; they do not assert a global gauge slice, since a gauge orbit may intersect the Lorenz slice more than once; such repeated intersections are Gribov copies. The ghost determinants omit the kernel of $\mathcal M$; infinitesimal stabilizers and residual gauge volumes are treated separately, with the final Cartan reduction retaining the Weyl quotient. The Euclidean contour takes the vector connections and real scalars on their Hermitian/real slices and pairs each matter scalar and auxiliary scalar with its conjugate partner; Euclidean fermions and their barred partners are independent Grassmann variables. The Cartan subalgebras are
$$\mathfrak h=\{\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_N):s_i\in\mathbb R\},\qquad \widehat{\mathfrak h}=\{\operatorname{diag}(\widehat s_1,\ldots,\widehat s_N):\widehat s_i\in\mathbb R\}.$$
The residual Weyl group $S_N\times S_N$ permutes the corresponding eigenvalues.

Choose a dimensionless smooth section $u\in C^\infty(M,S)$ with pointwise norm $h(u,u)=1$ satisfying $\nabla^S_Xu=\frac{i}{2r}\gamma(X^\flat)u$ for every smooth tangent vector field $X$, where $X^\flat=g(X,\cdot)$. This is the chosen normalized Killing spinor; its existence on the round sphere and its choice are part of the adopted source background. In the variations, $\nabla_\mu$ on spinors denotes $\nabla^S_{\partial_\mu}$. The profile $u$ and parameter $\epsilon$ are commuting spinors, while $Q$ is odd. The supersymmetry parameter in the variations below is $\epsilon=\sqrt r\,u$, so $[\epsilon]=r^{1/2}$ and $\nabla_\mu\epsilon=\frac{i}{2r}\gamma_\mu\epsilon$. Put $\gamma^{\mu\nu}=\frac12[\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu]$. The odd off-shell supersymmetry derivation $Q$ selected by this spinor acts on each vector multiplet, and identically on the hatted one, by
$$QA_\mu=-\frac{i}{2}\lambda^\dagger\gamma_\mu\epsilon,\quad Q\sigma=-\frac12\lambda^\dagger\epsilon,\quad QD=-\frac{i}{2}(D_\mu\lambda^\dagger)\gamma^\mu\epsilon+\frac{1}{4r}\lambda^\dagger\epsilon+\frac{i}{2}[\lambda^\dagger,\sigma]\epsilon,\quad Q\lambda=\left(-\frac12\gamma^{\mu\nu}F_{\mu\nu}-D+i\gamma^\mu D_\mu\sigma-\frac{\sigma}{r}\right)\epsilon,\quad Q\lambda^\dagger=0.$$
For each chiral multiplet $(\phi,\bar\phi,\psi,\bar\psi,F,\bar F)$ with $\Delta=\frac12$, it acts by
$$Q\phi=0,\quad Q\bar\phi=\bar\psi\epsilon,\quad Q\psi=\left(-i\gamma^\mu D_\mu\phi-i\sigma\phi+\frac{\phi}{2r}\right)\epsilon,\quad Q\bar\psi=\epsilon^T C\bar F,\quad QF=\epsilon^T C\left(-i\gamma^\mu D_\mu\psi+i\lambda\phi+i\sigma\psi\right),\quad Q\bar F=0.$$
Here barred chiral variables are the conjugate partners on the scalar/auxiliary contour and independent Euclidean Grassmann variables for fermions; all matrix-valued fields act in the chiral multiplet's stated representation. In the source's selected off-shell complex these transformations have $Q^2=0$. Extend $Q$ by zero on $c,\widehat c,\bar c,\bar{\widehat c},b,\widehat b$. The gauge-covariant BRST differential above then graded-anticommutes with $Q$, and the total odd derivation is $Q_{\rm gf}=Q+s$ with $Q_{\rm gf}^2=0$.

The gauge-fixing term used for localization is the **combined** insertion
$$S_{\mathrm{gf}}=Q_{\mathrm{gf}}\Psi_{\mathrm{gf}}=s\Psi_{\mathrm{gf}}-\int_{\mathbb S^3_r}d^3x\,\sqrt g\,\operatorname{tr}_N\left(\bar c\,\nabla^\mu QA_\mu+\bar{\widehat c}\,\nabla^\mu Q\widehat A_\mu\right).$$
The sign follows from the left graded Leibniz rule and the odd parity of each antighost; $Q$ annihilates antighosts and multipliers. The displayed $s\Psi_{\mathrm{gf}}$ alone is not the insertion asserted to be $Q_{\mathrm{gf}}$-closed. With the supplied off-shell algebra, $Q_{\mathrm{gf}}S_{\mathrm{gf}}=Q_{\mathrm{gf}}^2\Psi_{\mathrm{gf}}=0$. Thus the completed gauge-fixed action, rather than its BRST part alone, is the one used in the localization deformation. This is the combined gauge-fixing prescription in Kapustin–Willett–Yaakov §3.1, equations (3.10)–(3.13) in the current PDF (the equations numbered (30)–(33) in earlier numbering). Their extra supersymmetry variation is retained here explicitly; no unproved equality of two infinite-dimensional integrals is used to discard it.

With the radius restored, define the positive Hermitian inner product on the direct sum of the two matrix algebras by $\langle(X,\widehat X),(Y,\widehat Y)\rangle_+=\operatorname{tr}_N(X^\dagger Y)+\operatorname{tr}_N(\widehat X^\dagger\widehat Y)$. The source's positive gauge-sector deformation uses this form, independent of the signed Chern–Simons levels, and the odd gauge-invariant functional
$$V_{\rm vec}=\int_{\mathbb S^3_r}d^3x\,\sqrt g\,\left(\operatorname{tr}_N((Q\lambda)^\dagger\lambda)+\operatorname{tr}_N((Q\widehat\lambda)^\dagger\widehat\lambda)\right).$$
For the chiral-sector deformation, the unit-sphere source functional is multiplied by $r^{-1}$ so that the restored-radius functional below is dimensionless; this positive rescaling leaves its zero locus unchanged:
$$V_{\rm mat}=\frac{1}{r}\int_{\mathbb S^3_r}d^3x\,\sqrt g\sum_I\left((Q\psi_I)^\dagger\psi_I+\psi_I^\dagger(Q\bar\psi_I)^\dagger\right).$$
The sum over all chiral components is gauge invariant.
The source adds the $Q_{\rm gf}$-exact terms $tQ_{\rm gf}(V_{\rm vec}+V_{\rm mat})$ for a dimensionless parameter $t\geq0$, together with the completed gauge-fixing term $S_{\mathrm{gf}}=Q_{\mathrm{gf}}\Psi_{\mathrm{gf}}$. On the source localization locus, flat connections are gauge equivalent to zero on the stated trivial bundles over simply connected $\mathbb S^3$, matter and fermion fields vanish, and
$$\sigma=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_N),\quad \widehat\sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\widehat s_1,\ldots,\widehat s_N),\quad D=-\sigma/r,\quad\widehat D=-\widehat\sigma/r.$$
The corresponding one-loop factors are the source's Gaussian boson/fermion/ghost determinant ratios about this locus. For the positive-spectrum determinant convention, fix a smooth finite-rank Hermitian complex bundle $E\to M$, with a fixed smooth compatible connection, and the Hilbert space $\mathcal H=L^2(M,E)$ with inner product $\langle f,g\rangle=\int_M h_E(f,g)\,d\operatorname{vol}_g$. Let $L_0:C^\infty(M,E)\to C^\infty(M,E)$ be a differential operator of positive integer order $m_L$ with smooth coefficients. In a local expression $L_0=\sum_{|\alpha|\le m_L}a_\alpha(x)\partial^\alpha$, its principal symbol is $\sigma_{m_L}(L_0)(x,\xi)=\sum_{|\alpha|=m_L}a_\alpha(x)(i\xi)^\alpha$; ellipticity means this endomorphism of $E_x$ is invertible for every nonzero real cotangent vector $\xi\in T_x^*M$. Use the realization $Lf=L_0f$ in the distributional sense with domain $\mathcal D(L)=H^{m_L}(M,E)\subset\mathcal H$, where $H^{m_L}$ is the completion of smooth sections in the norm squared $\sum_{j=0}^{m_L}\int_M|\nabla^j f|^2\,d\operatorname{vol}_g$. Require that $L$ is densely defined and closed, that its Hilbert-space adjoint has $\mathcal D(L^*)=\mathcal D(L)$ and $L^*=L$, and that $\langle f,Lf\rangle\ge c_L\|f\|^2$ for all $f\in\mathcal D(L)$ for some $c_L>0$. These are the self-adjointness and strict positivity hypotheses. Require an orthonormal eigenbasis with positive eigenvalues $\nu_j$ of finite multiplicity tending to infinity, listed with multiplicity and with no kernel; no spectral-existence theorem is being inferred from terminology. Assume $\sum_j\nu_j^{-s_0}<\infty$ for some real $s_0>0$. With $[L]=r^{-m_L}$, set $\widetilde L=r^{m_L}L$ so that its eigenvalues $\widetilde\nu_j=r^{m_L}\nu_j$ are dimensionless. Define $\zeta_{\widetilde L}(s)=\sum_j\widetilde\nu_j^{-s}$ initially for $\operatorname{Re}s>s_0$, using the real logarithm of each positive eigenvalue; when it has a meromorphic continuation holomorphic at $s=0$, set $\det_\zeta\widetilde L=\exp(-\zeta_{\widetilde L}'(0))$. For an operator with a finite-dimensional kernel, the same convention on its orthogonal complement defines a primed determinant provided the remaining positive spectrum and continuation satisfy the stated hypotheses. A primed determinant omits the kernel only; its zero modes are treated separately, with the finite Cartan modes integrated and gauge stabilizer modes removed by the residual quotient. The source's phase prescription for fermionic or other nonpositive/complex fluctuation operators and for the oscillatory Chern–Simons Gaussian is part of the cited calculation; the positive-spectrum formula above is not applied to those operators.

In the Kapustin–Willett–Yaakov Euclidean convention, let $\mathcal S_{\rm CS}$ be the sum of the two real functionals displayed above, let $S_{\rm chiral}$ be the sum of the four chiral kinetic actions, and let $S_W$ be the off-shell interaction just specified. Define the Euclidean action and weight by
$$S_E=S_{\rm chiral}+S_W-i\mathcal S_{\rm CS},\qquad e^{-S_E}=e^{\,i\mathcal S_{\rm CS}-S_{\rm chiral}-S_W}.$$
At the stated localization locus this gives
$$i\mathcal S_{\rm CS}=-i\pi k\left(\sum_i(rs_i)^2-\sum_i(r\widehat s_i)^2\right),$$
so the real Cartan integral has the oscillatory classical phase used in the Example. In particular, the real functional $S_{\rm CS}$ enters the Euclidean weight with the displayed factor $+i$.

Before gauge fixing, the orbit-normalized functional integral is only the formal expression
$$Z_{\mathrm{formal}}=\frac{1}{\operatorname{Vol}(\mathcal G)}\int_{\mathcal C}[D\Phi]_{\mathrm{formal}}\,e^{-S_E[\Phi]},$$
where $\operatorname{Vol}(\mathcal G)$ is a formal normalization of the gauge-orbit volume, not a defined finite number, and $\mathcal C$ is the source Euclidean contour. The local Lorenz-gauge representation is symbolically the integral with the gauge-fixing delta functional $\delta[\mathcal F]$ and $\det{}'\mathcal M_{A,\widehat A}$, whose conventional multiplier/ghost part is $s\Psi_{\mathrm{gf}}$. In the localization representation this is completed to $S_{\mathrm{gf}}=Q_{\mathrm{gf}}\Psi_{\mathrm{gf}}$, including the antighost–supersymmetry term displayed above; the multiplier constraint and residual quotient are retained. The orbit-volume division is implemented once. No quotient notation $\mathcal C/\mathcal G$ or second volume divisor is added. Residual stabilizers and the Weyl quotient are treated separately as specified above. The source calculation assumes that its gauge-fixed measure and contour are $Q_{\mathrm{gf}}$-invariant and that the deformation introduces no anomalous Jacobian (a multiplicative change of the formal measure under $Q_{\mathrm{gf}}$) or surface contribution at the boundary of field space. These are adopted formal field-theory inputs: this postulate does not construct an infinite-dimensional measure, prove convergence of the localization limit, or assert a theorem for arbitrary three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ models.",

          "statement": "Assume AC. Let $V=\\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\\mathbb C^N$, $N\\ge1$, $k\\ge0$, with their standard Hermitian products. Define the raw moment maps\n\n$$\\mu_{\\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\\qquad \\mu_{\\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\\dagger]+II^\\dagger-J^\\dagger J,$$\n\nand assume $\\mu_{\\mathbb C}=0$. Put $K=V\\oplus V\\oplus W$. For $z=(z_1,z_2)\\in\\mathbb C^2$ put\n\n$$a_z=(B_1-z_1,B_2-z_2,J)^T,\\qquad b_z=(-B_2^\\dagger+\\bar z_2,B_1^\\dagger-\\bar z_1,I^\\dagger)^T,\\qquad D_z=\\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\\dagger\\\\a_z^\\dagger\\end{pmatrix}.$$\n\nThen\n\n$$D_zD_z^\\dagger=\\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\\dagger b_z&\\mu_{\\mathbb C}\\\\\\mu_{\\mathbb C}^\\dagger&a_z^\\dagger a_z\\end{pmatrix},\\qquad b_z^\\dagger b_z-a_z^\\dagger a_z=\\mu_{\\mathbb R}.$$\n\nThe maps $b_z^\\dagger$ are onto for every $z$ exactly when the datum is stable; the maps $a_z$ are injective for every $z$ exactly when it is costable. Consequently, when both moments vanish, regularity is equivalent to $D_z$ being onto for every $z$. On this locus $f_z=a_z^\\dagger a_z=b_z^\\dagger b_z$ is positive definite and\n\n$$P_z=1-D_z^\\dagger\\operatorname{diag}(f_z^{-1},f_z^{-1})D_z$$\n\nis the smooth orthogonal projection onto a rank-$N$ bundle over $\\mathbb R^4$. The projection connection $\\nabla=P\\,d$ is unitary and satisfies $F^+=0$ for the positive stereographic orientation $dx^0\\wedge dx^1\\wedge dx^2\\wedge dx^3$, where $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$.\n\nIn homogeneous coordinates $[\\lambda_1:\\lambda_2:\\mu_1:\\mu_2]$ on $\\mathbb P^3$, put $A=B_1\\lambda_1-B_2^\\dagger\\lambda_2-\\mu_1$, $C=B_2\\lambda_1+B_1^\\dagger\\lambda_2-\\mu_2$ and\n\n$$\\alpha=(A,C,J\\lambda_1+I^\\dagger\\lambda_2)^T,\\qquad\\beta=(-C,A,I\\lambda_1-J^\\dagger\\lambda_2).$$\n\nThe polynomial identity is $\\beta\\alpha=\\lambda_1^2\\mu_{\\mathbb C}+\\lambda_1\\lambda_2\\mu_{\\mathbb R}-\\lambda_2^2\\mu_{\\mathbb C}^\\dagger$. With $\\sigma(\\lambda_1,\\lambda_2,\\mu_1,\\mu_2)=(-\\bar\\lambda_2,\\bar\\lambda_1,-\\bar\\mu_2,\\bar\\mu_1)$, one has $\\beta(v)=\\alpha(\\sigma v)^\\dagger$. The real line over $z$ is $\\mu_1=z_1\\lambda_1-\\bar z_2\\lambda_2$, $\\mu_2=z_2\\lambda_1+\\bar z_1\\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\\lambda_1=\\lambda_2=0$. For regular zero-moment data these maps form a holomorphic bundle monad, trivial on each real line, with middle cohomology on the line over $z$ canonically $\\ker D_z$. Its framing at infinity is $W$. The torus acts on the homogeneous coordinates by $(\\lambda_1,t_1t_2\\lambda_2,t_1\\mu_1,t_2\\mu_2)$ and on the raw data by $(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$; the monad isomorphism has source, middle and target factors $(t_1t_2)^{-1}$, $\\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)$ and $1$, respectively. It preserves the framing representation $W$ with weights $e_\\alpha^{-1}$.\n\nThis proves a forward raw block construction.           "statement": "Use the dual-number scheme, relative projective-space charts, finite locally free sheaves and twisting sheaves as defined, respectively, in the four suppliers listed under Definition references, with the inherited AC convention for the twisting-sheaf construction. Let $A=\\mathbb C[\\epsilon]/(\\epsilon^2)$ and equip it with the conjugate-linear involution $\\overline{a+b\\epsilon}=\\bar a+\\bar b\\epsilon$. Its reduction is the quotient map $A\\to\\mathbb C$ sending $\\epsilon$ to zero. For every $r\\in\\mathbb R$, the map $\\rho_r:A\\to A$ fixing $\\mathbb C$ and sending $\\epsilon$ to $r\\epsilon$ preserves this involution.\n\nA **first-order family of positive real linear monads of dimensions $(k,2k+N,k)$** is a three-term complex of locally free sheaves on $\\mathbb P^3_A=\\operatorname{Proj}A[\\lambda_1,\\lambda_2,\\mu_1,\\mu_2]$,\n$$\\mathcal O(-1)\\otimes_A U_A\\xrightarrow{\\alpha_A}\\mathcal O\\otimes_A S_A\\xrightarrow{\\beta_A}\\mathcal O(1)\\otimes_A U'_A,$$\nwhere $U_A,S_A,U'_A$ are free $A$-modules of ranks $k,2k+N,k$, each map is homogeneous linear in $(\\lambda_1,\\lambda_2,\\mu_1,\\mu_2)$, $\\beta_A\\alpha_A=0$, $\\alpha_A$ is a locally split injection, $\\beta_A$ is a locally split surjection, and $F_A=\\ker\\beta_A/\\operatorname{im}\\alpha_A$ is locally free of rank $N$. The two short exact sequences defined by the kernel and image split locally; hence their formation and the middle cohomology commute with reduction $A\\to\\mathbb C$. The reduced complex is therefore an ordinary linear monad on $\\mathbb P^3_\\mathbb C$.\n\nThe **first-order locally-free/base-change range** used here further requires that $H^0(\\mathbb P^3_A,F_A)$ is a free $A$-module and reduction identifies it with $H^0(\\mathbb P^3_\\mathbb C,F_0)$, where $F_0=F_A\\otimes_A\\mathbb C$. The image in $S_A$ of the map from the four coefficient copies of $U_A$ under $\\alpha_A$ is a direct summand and reduces to the corresponding coefficient-image subspace of $S_0$. For each real twistor line $\\ell$ in the reduced projective space, the restriction of $F_A$ to $\\ell_A=\\ell\\times_{\\mathbb C}\\operatorname{Spec}A$ is trivial of rank $N$, and reduction identifies its global sections with $H^0(\\ell,F_0|_\\ell)$. These conditions state the precise global, coefficient-image, and line-section base-change range; no arbitrary analytic family or algebraization assertion is included.\n\nExtend the coordinate map $j(\\lambda_1,\\lambda_2,\\mu_1,\\mu_2)=(-\\bar\\lambda_2,\\bar\\lambda_1,-\\bar\\mu_2,\\bar\\mu_1)$ semilinearly using the involution of $A$; write $\\widetilde\\sigma$ for its projective action over $A$ and $\\sigma$ for its reduction. Since $j^2=-1$, both projective actions square to the identity and preserve each real twistor line. A **real twistor line** means the projectivization of a $j$-invariant complex two-plane in $\\mathbb C^4$. Equivalently these are the finite lines\n$$\\mu_1=z_1\\lambda_1-\\bar z_2\\lambda_2,\\qquad \\mu_2=z_2\\lambda_1+\\bar z_1\\lambda_2,\\qquad (z_1,z_2)\\in\\mathbb C^2,$$\ntogether with $\\ell_\\infty=\\{\\lambda_1=\\lambda_2=0\\}$. Indeed a nonzero vector $v$ and $jv$ are complex-linearly independent because $j^2=-1$; they span the invariant plane. If its $\\lambda$ projection is nonzero, that projection and its quaternionic conjugate give an invertible two-by-two matrix with determinant $|\\lambda_1|^2+|\\lambda_2|^2$, so it has exactly the displayed graph form; if the projection is zero the plane is the $\\mu$ plane. Each fixed-line restriction above means the corresponding constant thickening $\\ell_A$.\n\nFor an $A$-locally free sheaf $G$, write $D_A(G):=(\\widetilde\\sigma^*\\overline G)^\\vee$, where $\\overline G$ has its scalar action conjugated by $a\\mapsto\\bar a$ and $(-)^\\vee=\\mathcal Hom_{\\mathcal O}(-,\\mathcal O)$. On the reduction, write $D(F_0):=(\\sigma^*\\overline{F_0})^\\vee$. A first-order real structure is an $\\mathcal O_{\\mathbb P^3_A}$-linear isomorphism $h_A:F_A\\to D_A(F_A)$ fixed by the canonical double-dual identification $D_A^2(F_A)\\cong F_A$. Its reduction $h_0:F_0\\to D(F_0)$ gives fiber pairings\n$$b_x(v,w):=h_{0,x}(v)(\\overline w),\\qquad v\\in(F_0)_x,\\quad w\\in(F_0)_{\\sigma x},$$\nwhich are linear in $v$, conjugate-linear in $w$, and satisfy $b_{\\sigma x}(w,v)=\\overline{b_x(v,w)}$. For a $\\sigma$-invariant real line $\\ell$ and $s,t\\in H^0(\\ell,F_0|_\\ell)$, the induced line form is the constant value of the function $x\\mapsto b_x(s(x),t(\\sigma x))$; constancy is part of the stated real-structure condition. It is first-slot-linear and Hermitian by the displayed symmetry. Positivity means $b_\\ell(s,s)>0$ for every nonzero $s$. A unitary framing at infinity is an isometric isomorphism $F_A|_{\\ell_\\infty}\\cong (A\\otimes_\\mathbb C W)\\otimes_A\\mathcal O_{\\ell_\\infty}$, where $\\ell_\\infty=\\{\\lambda_1=\\lambda_2=0\\}$ and $W=\\mathbb C^N$ has its standard first-slot-linear Hermitian form.\n\nAn isomorphism of such families is an $A$-linear chain isomorphism that intertwines the $\\sigma$-Hermitian pairings and the framing. No order or positivity is assigned to elements of $A$ with nonzero nilpotent part: positivity is required only after reduction.
