          "proof_strategy": "direct",
          "statement": "Let $k,N\\in\\mathbb Z_{\\ge0}$, and let $\\mathcal F$ be the locally free algebraic middle cohomology of a linear monad\n$$\n\\mathcal O_{\\mathbb P^3}(-1)^{\\oplus k}\\longrightarrow\\mathcal O_{\\mathbb P^3}^{\\oplus(2k+N)}\\longrightarrow\\mathcal O_{\\mathbb P^3}(1)^{\\oplus k}\n$$\non $\\mathbb P^3_\\mathbb C$, with exactness at both ends.\n\nFor algebraic sheaf cohomology, write $H^q(\\mathbb P^3,\\mathcal G)$ for the right-derived global-sections group. If these groups are finite-dimensional and vanish for all sufficiently large $q$, define the algebraic Euler characteristic by $\\chi(\\mathcal G)=\\sum_{q\\ge0}(-1)^q\\dim_{\\mathbb C}H^q(\\mathbb P^3,\\mathcal G)$. Let $H_{\\rm alg}=c_1^{\\rm alg}(\\mathcal O_{\\mathbb P^3}(1))$ in the Chow ring and let $H_{\\rm top}=c_1^{\\rm top}(\\mathcal O_{\\mathbb P^3}(1))$ in singular cohomology. The hyperplane cycle map $\\operatorname{cl}:A^1(\\mathbb P^3)\\to H^2(\\mathbb P^3;\\mathbb Z)$ identifies $H_{\\rm alg}$ with $H_{\\rm top}$; write $H$ for either class in the corresponding formula. The algebraic Chern character is $N-kH_{\\rm alg}^2$, the algebraic first Chern class is zero, the algebraic second Chern class is $kH_{\\rm alg}^2$, and the algebraic Euler characteristic is $N-2k$. The analytification of $\\mathcal F$ has total topological Chern class $1+kH_{\\rm top}^2$ through degree six and topological Chern character $N-kH_{\\rm top}^2$.\n\nLet $\\jmath:\\mathbb C^4\\to\\mathbb C^4$ be the conjugate-linear map\n$$\\jmath(\\lambda_1,\\lambda_2,\\mu_1,\\mu_2)=(-\\bar\\lambda_2,\\bar\\lambda_1,-\\bar\\mu_2,\\bar\\mu_1),\\qquad \\jmath^2=-1.$$\nUse $\\mathbb H=\\mathbb C\\oplus\\mathbb C\\mathbf j$, where $\\mathbf j^2=-1$ and $\\mathbf j a=\\bar a\\mathbf j$ for $a\\in\\mathbb C$, and identify $\\mathbb C^4$ with the right quaternionic vector space $\\mathbb H^2$ by\n$$ (\\lambda_1,\\lambda_2,\\mu_1,\\mu_2)\\longmapsto(\\lambda_1+\\bar\\lambda_2\\mathbf j,\\ \\mu_1+\\bar\\mu_2\\mathbf j).$$\nUnder this identification, right multiplication by $\\mathbf j$ is $\\jmath$. Give $\\mathbb H\\mathbb P^1=(\\mathbb H^2\\setminus\\{0\\})/\\mathbb H^\\times$ its standard smooth quotient structure; it is the 4-sphere and its points are the one-dimensional right-$\\mathbb H$ subspaces of $\\mathbb H^2$. The **quaternionic quotient map** is the smooth map\n$$\\pi:\\mathbb P(\\mathbb C^4)\\longrightarrow\\mathbb H\\mathbb P^1,\\qquad [\\lambda_1:\\lambda_2:\\mu_1:\\mu_2]\\longmapsto[(\\lambda_1+\\bar\\lambda_2\\mathbf j,\\ \\mu_1+\\bar\\mu_2\\mathbf j)]_{\\mathbb H}.$$\nEquivalently, $\\pi([v])=\\operatorname{span}_{\\mathbb C}(v,\\jmath v)$, a $\\jmath$-invariant complex two-plane. This is well-defined because $\\jmath(cv)=\\bar c\\,\\jmath v$ for $c\\in\\mathbb C$ and $v,\\jmath v$ are complex-linearly independent when $v\\ne0$ and $\\jmath^2=-1$. Its fiber over a quaternionic line $L$ is $\\mathbb P_{\\mathbb C}(L)\\cong\\mathbb P^1(\\mathbb C)$. In the finite chart with $\\lambda=\\lambda_1+\\bar\\lambda_2\\mathbf j\\ne0$ and $z=\\mu\\lambda^{-1}=z_1+\\bar z_2\\mathbf j$, the fiber equations are\n$$\\mu_1=z_1\\lambda_1-\\bar z_2\\lambda_2,\\qquad \\mu_2=z_2\\lambda_1+\\bar z_1\\lambda_2,$$\nand the fiber over the remaining point is $\\ell_\\infty=\\{\\lambda_1=\\lambda_2=0\\}$. Orient each fiber by its complex orientation. Write $z_1=x^0+ix^1$ and $z_2=x^2+ix^3$, so the chart orientation is $dx^0\\wedge dx^1\\wedge dx^2\\wedge dx^3$; orient $S^4$ so this positive stereographic chart followed by the fiber orientation induces the complex orientation of $\\mathbb P^3$. Since the base and fiber dimensions are $4$ and $2$, respectively, reversing these orientation factors has sign $(-1)^{4\\cdot2}=+1$, so this also agrees with the fiber-first convention. Let $u\\in H^4(S^4;\\mathbb Z)$ be the positive point class for this orientation. Then $\\pi^*u=H_{\\rm top}^2$.           "statement": "Use the complex field $\\mathbb C$ with conjugation $z\\mapsto\\overline z$. Fix an integer $N\\ge1$. Let $S=\\mathbb C^2$ have standard basis $s_1,s_2$. For a complex vector space $W$, its conjugate vector space $\\overline W$ consists of symbols $\\overline w$ for $w\\in W$, with addition $\\overline w+\\overline v=\\overline{w+v}$ and scalar action $\\lambda\\overline w=\\overline{\\overline\\lambda w}$. Set $\\dot S=\\overline S$ with dotted basis $\\dot s_{\\dot1}=\\overline{s_1}$ and $\\dot s_{\\dot2}=\\overline{s_2}$. Let $F=\\mathbb C^N$ have standard basis $f_1,\\ldots,f_N$, and let $F^*$ be its complex-linear dual with dual basis $f^1,\\ldots,f^N$ and scalar action $(\\lambda\\ell)(v)=\\lambda\\ell(v)$. All tensor products are over $\\mathbb C$, with scalar action $\\lambda(v\\otimes w)=(\\lambda v)\\otimes w=v\\otimes(\\lambda w)$ and product bases formed from the displayed bases. Define $\\Lambda^2F=(F\\otimes_{\\mathbb C}F)/\\operatorname{span}_{\\mathbb C}\\{v\\otimes v:v\\in F\\}$; its basis is $f_I\\wedge f_J$ for $1\\le I<J\\le N$, with quotient scalar action. Its conjugate $\\overline{\\Lambda^2F}$ has basis $\\overline{f_I\\wedge f_J}$ and the conjugate scalar action just defined. For $N=1$ these exterior-square spaces are zero. In the displayed bases, $\\mathfrak{sl}(S)=\\{A\\in\\operatorname{End}_{\\mathbb C}(S):\\operatorname{tr}A=0\\}$ and $\\mathfrak{sl}(\\dot S)=\\{B\\in\\operatorname{End}_{\\mathbb C}(\\dot S):\\operatorname{tr}B=0\\}$. Put $\\epsilon_{12}=\\epsilon_{\\dot1\\dot2}=1$ and $\\epsilon_{21}=\\epsilon_{\\dot2\\dot1}=-1$, with zero diagonal. The complex even space is\n\n$$\\mathfrak g_{\\bar0}=\\bigl(\\mathfrak{sl}(S)\\oplus\\mathfrak{sl}(\\dot S)\\bigr)\\oplus V\\oplus C_N,\\qquad V=S\\otimes\\dot S,\\qquad C_N=\\Lambda^2F\\oplus\\overline{\\Lambda^2F}.$$\n\nWrite $T_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta}=s_\\alpha\\otimes\\dot s_{\\dot\\beta}$ for the basis of $V$. The listed central generators form a basis of $C_N$: $Z^{IJ}$ corresponds to $f_I\\wedge f_J$ and $\\bar Z_{IJ}$ to $\\overline{f_I\\wedge f_J}$ for $1\\le I<J\\le N$; extend them by antisymmetry in the flavor indices and set their diagonal entries to zero. The complex odd space is\n\n$$\\mathfrak g_{\\bar1}=(S\\otimes F)\\oplus(\\dot S\\otimes F^*),$$\n\nwith basis $Q^I_\\alpha=s_\\alpha\\otimes f_I$ and $\\bar Q_{\\dot\\alpha I}=\\dot s_{\\dot\\alpha}\\otimes f^I$. A homogeneous vector has parity $|x|\\in\\{0,1\\}$. The bracket is complex-bilinear, preserves parity, and obeys $[x,y]=-(-1)^{|x||y|}[y,x]$. Its complete nonzero table, apart from the graded-skew consequences, is\n\n$$[ (A,B),(A',B') ]=([A,A'],[B,B']),\\qquad [(A,B),T]= (A\\otimes I+I\\otimes B)T,$$\n\n$$[(A,B),Q^I_\\alpha]=A^\\gamma{}_{\\alpha}Q^I_\\gamma,\\qquad [(A,B),\\bar Q_{\\dot\\alpha I}]=B^{\\dot\\gamma}{}_{\\dot\\alpha}\\bar Q_{\\dot\\gamma I},$$\n\nHere $A^\\gamma{}_{\\alpha}$ is the entry in row $\\gamma$, column $\\alpha$, so $As_\\alpha=\\sum_\\gamma A^\\gamma{}_{\\alpha}s_\\gamma$; dotted entries use the same convention. Thus on the translation basis the tensor action is $[(A,B),T_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta}]=\\sum_\\gamma A^\\gamma{}_{\\alpha}T_{\\gamma\\dot\\beta}+\\sum_{\\dot\\gamma}B^{\\dot\\gamma}{}_{\\dot\\beta}T_{\\alpha\\dot\\gamma}$.\n\n$$\\{Q^I_\\alpha,\\bar Q_{\\dot\\beta J}\\}=-2\\delta^I{}_J T_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta},\\qquad \\{Q^I_\\alpha,Q^J_\\beta\\}=2\\epsilon_{\\alpha\\beta}Z^{IJ},\\qquad \\{\\bar Q_{\\dot\\alpha I},\\bar Q_{\\dot\\beta J}\\}=2\\epsilon_{\\dot\\alpha\\dot\\beta}\\bar Z_{IJ}.$$\n\nAll other brackets vanish: $V$ and $C_N$ are abelian, $C_N$ is central, and $V$ brackets trivially with the odd space. The two antisymmetric factors in each equal-chirality odd bracket make that bracket symmetric in the combined spinor-flavor labels. The Lie-superalgebra and real-form properties are established by the local Jacobi result.\n\nDefine a conjugate-linear involution $*$ on the generators by\n\n$$ (A,B)^*=(-\\overline B,-\\overline A),\\quad Q^I_\\alpha{}^*=\\bar Q_{\\dot\\alpha I},\\quad \\bar Q_{\\dot\\alpha I}{}^*=Q^I_\\alpha,\\quad T_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta}^*=T_{\\beta\\dot\\alpha},\\quad (Z^{IJ})^*=\\bar Z_{IJ},\\quad (\\bar Z_{IJ})^*=Z^{IJ}.$$\n\nIt uses the operator-adjoint convention $[x,y]^*=-(-1)^{|x||y|}[x^*,y^*]$. The associated real Lie superalgebra is the fixed space of the conjugate-linear map $\\tau(x)=-x^*$ on even elements and $\\tau(x)=i x^*$ on odd elements. Its real Lorentz algebra is the fixed diagonal copy of $\\mathfrak{sl}(2,\\mathbb C)$; its real translation generators are the $\\tau$-fixed skew-Hermitian bispinors. The star-fixed translation coordinates defined below are abstract elements of the complex algebra; their multiples by $i$ form a real basis of the tau-fixed translation space.\n\nFor the metric convention $\\eta=\\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, put $\\sigma^0=I_2$ and\n\n$$\\sigma^1=\\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\\\1&0\\end{pmatrix},\\qquad \\sigma^2=\\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\\\i&0\\end{pmatrix},\\qquad \\sigma^3=\\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\\\0&-1\\end{pmatrix},\\qquad \\bar\\sigma^0=I_2,\\qquad \\bar\\sigma^j=-\\sigma^j.$$\n\nThey obey\n\n$$\\sigma^\\mu\\bar\\sigma^\\nu+\\sigma^\\nu\\bar\\sigma^\\mu=-2\\eta^{\\mu\\nu}I_2.$$\n\nDefine abstract translation coordinates $p_0=(T_{1\\dot1}+T_{2\\dot2})/2$, $p_1=(T_{1\\dot2}+T_{2\\dot1})/2$, $p_2=(T_{2\\dot1}-T_{1\\dot2})/(2i)$, and $p_3=(T_{1\\dot1}-T_{2\\dot2})/2$. Then $T_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta}=\\sigma^\\mu_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta}p_\\mu$, $p_\\mu^*=p_\\mu$, and $\\tau(ip_\\mu)=ip_\\mu$. A representation of the complex supertranslation algebra $\\mathfrak t=V\\oplus C_N\\oplus\\mathfrak g_{\\bar1}$ on a graded complex vector space $\\mathcal D$ means a parity-preserving complex-linear map $\\rho:\\mathfrak t\\to\\operatorname{End}_{\\mathbb C}(\\mathcal D)$ preserving the bracket, where the target bracket on homogeneous endomorphisms is $[X,Y]=XY-(-1)^{|X||Y|}YX$. Write $P_\\mu=\\rho(p_\\mu)$ and use the charge symbols for their images. Thus $\\rho(T_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta})=\\sigma^\\mu_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta}P_\\mu$ and the represented mixed relation is $\\{Q^I_\\alpha,\\bar Q_{\\dot\\beta J}\\}=-2\\sigma^\\mu_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta}P_\\mu\\delta^I{}_J$, with $P_\\mu=\\eta_{\\mu\\nu}P^\\nu$. Complex linearity gives $\\rho(ip_\\mu)=iP_\\mu$, hence $-i\\rho(ip_\\mu)=P_\\mu$. For a real number $M>0$, a massive rest module here means such a supertranslation representation with $P^0=M I_{\\mathcal D}$ and $P^j=0$ for $j=1,2,3$. Consequently $P_0=-M I_{\\mathcal D}$ and its mixed anticommutator is $2M\\delta_{\\alpha\\dot\\beta}\\delta^I{}_J I_{\\mathcal D}$. This is an algebraic specialization, with no assertion of a Hilbert adjoint or a spectral fiber. Here $N$ counts left Weyl spinors; the scalar central-charge matrix is antisymmetric and therefore vanishes for $N=1$. Tensorial or topological extensions are outside this scalar-central-charge algebra. The round-sphere component action for one chiral multiplet $(\phi,\psi,F)$ of $R$-charge $\Delta=\tfrac12$, in the representation determined by its bifundamental type, is

The representation-valued $\sigma,D,\lambda$ in this expression act by the first-factor action minus the second-factor action. Sum this action over the four chiral multiplets.

The adopted $\mathcal N=2$ superpotential is

Identify $\\operatorname{Mat}_N(\\mathbb C)$ with $\\mathbb R^{2N^2}$ by the real and imaginary matrix entries, and let $\\operatorname{Herm}_N=\\{H:H^*=H\\}$ have its induced real vector-space structure. Equip $U(N)=\\{U:U^*U=I_N\\}$ with the embedded regular-level-set structure at $I_N$ of the smooth map $F:\\operatorname{GL}_N(\\mathbb C)\\to\\operatorname{Herm}_N$, $F(U)=U^*U$, where $\\operatorname{GL}_N(\\mathbb C)=\\{U:\\det U\\ne0\\}$. Equip $S^1=\\{z\\in\\mathbb C:|z|=1\\}$ with its embedded circle structure and $SU(N)$ with the embedded regular-level-set structure at $1$ of $\\det:U(N)\\to S^1$. These are the embedded structures in the stated real matrix space. Its real Lie algebra is $\\mathfrak{su}(N):=\\{X\\in\\operatorname{Mat}_N(\\mathbb C):X^*=-X,\\ \\operatorname{tr}X=0\\}$ with bracket $[X,Y]=XY-YX$. The standard unitary representation is the map $\\rho:SU(N)\\to U(\\mathbb C^N,h)$ defined by $\\rho(U)v=Uv$, where $h(v,w)=\\sum_{j=1}^N\\overline{v_j}w_j$ and $U(\\mathbb C^N,h)$ consists of the complex-linear maps preserving $h$.           "id": "lem-qftx-parametric-vector-bundle-section-smoothing",
          "reference": "items/lem-qftx-parametric-vector-bundle-section-smoothing.md#Statement",
          "domain": "mathematics",
          "library": "mathematics",
          "statement": "Let $X$ be a compact finite-dimensional smooth manifold, $K\\subseteq X$ a closed smooth submanifold with a chosen collar, $M$ a compact smooth manifold, and $E\\to M$ a finite-rank smooth real vector bundle. Let $s:X\\times M\\to E$ be a continuous family of sections, meaning $s(x,m)\\in E_m$ and $(x,m)\\mapsto s(x,m)$ is continuous. Assume $x\\mapsto s(x,\\cdot)$ is continuous in the uniform topology, its restriction to $K$ is continuous in the $C^\\infty$ section topology, and for distinct marked points $m_1,\\ldots,m_q\\in M$ the values $s(x,m_i)=v_i\\in E_{m_i}$ are independent of $x$. For every $\\varepsilon>0$ there is a family $\\widetilde s:X\\to\\Gamma^\\infty(E)$ continuous in the $C^\\infty$ topology, equal to $s$ on $K$, equal to $v_i$ at every $m_i$, and satisfying $\\sup(\\{0\\}\\cup\\{\\|\\widetilde s(x,m)-s(x,m)\\|:(x,m)\\in X\\times M\\})<\\varepsilon$ for any fixed bundle norm. The straight-line homotopy in each vector fiber from $s$ to $\\widetilde s$ fixes $K$ and all marked values.",
          "category": "quantum-field-theory-mathematics"

          "library": "mathematics",
          "statement": "Let $f:S^3\\to S^2$ be a based continuous map. Give $S^2$ an orientation and give the attached $4$-cell its chosen orientation.           "statement": "Assume AC. Let $V=\\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\\mathbb C^N$, $N\\ge1$, $k\\ge0$, with their standard Hermitian products. For $z=(z_1,z_2)\\in\\mathbb C^2$ put\n\n$$a_z=(B_1-z_1,B_2-z_2,J)^T,\\qquad b_z=(-B_2^\\dagger+\\bar z_2,B_1^\\dagger-\\bar z_1,I^\\dagger)^T,\\qquad D_z=\\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\\dagger\\\\a_z^\\dagger\\end{pmatrix}.$$\n\nThen\n\n$$D_zD_z^\\dagger=\\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\\dagger b_z&\\mu_{\\mathbb C}\\\\\\mu_{\\mathbb C}^\\dagger&a_z^\\dagger a_z\\end{pmatrix},\\qquad b_z^\\dagger b_z-a_z^\\dagger a_z=\\mu_{\\mathbb R}.$$\n\nThe maps $b_z^\\dagger$ are onto for every $z$ exactly when the datum is stable; the maps $a_z$ are injective for every $z$ exactly when it is costable. Consequently, when both moments vanish, regularity is equivalent to $D_z$ being onto for every $z$. On this locus $f_z=a_z^\\dagger a_z=b_z^\\dagger b_z$ is positive definite and\n\n$$P_z=1-D_z^\\dagger\\operatorname{diag}(f_z^{-1},f_z^{-1})D_z$$\n\nis the smooth orthogonal projection onto a rank-$N$ bundle over $\\mathbb R^4$. For regular zero-moment data these maps form a holomorphic bundle monad, trivial on each real line, with middle cohomology on the line over $z$ canonically $\\ker D_z$. Its framing at infinity is $W$. The torus acts on the homogeneous coordinates by $(\\lambda_1,t_1t_2\\lambda_2,t_1\\mu_1,t_2\\mu_2)$ and on the raw data by $(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$; the monad isomorphism has source, middle and target factors $(t_1t_2)^{-1}$, $\\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)$ and $1$, respectively.           "statement": "Use the dual-number scheme, relative projective-space charts, finite locally free sheaves and twisting sheaves as defined, respectively, in the four suppliers listed under Definition references, with the inherited AC convention for the twisting-sheaf construction. Let $A=\\mathbb C[\\epsilon]/(\\epsilon^2)$ and equip it with the conjugate-linear involution $\\overline{a+b\\epsilon}=\\bar a+\\bar b\\epsilon$. Its reduction is the quotient map $A\\to\\mathbb C$ sending $\\epsilon$ to zero. For every $r\\in\\mathbb R$, the map $\\rho_r:A\\to A$ fixing $\\mathbb C$ and sending $\\epsilon$ to $r\\epsilon$ preserves this involution.\n\nA **first-order family of positive real linear monads of dimensions $(k,2k+N,k)$** is a three-term complex of locally free sheaves on $\\mathbb P^3_A=\\operatorname{Proj}A[\\lambda_1,\\lambda_2,\\mu_1,\\mu_2]$,\n$$\\mathcal O(-1)\\otimes_A U_A\\xrightarrow{\\alpha_A}\\mathcal O\\otimes_A S_A\\xrightarrow{\\beta_A}\\mathcal O(1)\\otimes_A U'_A,$$\nwhere $U_A,S_A,U'_A$ are free $A$-modules of ranks $k,2k+N,k$, each map is homogeneous linear in $(\\lambda_1,\\lambda_2,\\mu_1,\\mu_2)$, $\\beta_A\\alpha_A=0$, $\\alpha_A$ is a locally split injection, $\\beta_A$ is a locally split surjection, and $F_A=\\ker\\beta_A/\\operatorname{im}\\alpha_A$ is locally free of rank $N$. The two short exact sequences defined by the kernel and image split locally; hence their formation and the middle cohomology commute with reduction $A\\to\\mathbb C$. The reduced complex is therefore an ordinary linear monad on $\\mathbb P^3_\\mathbb C$.\n\nThe **first-order locally-free/base-change range** used here further requires that $H^0(\\mathbb P^3_A,F_A)$ is a free $A$-module and reduction identifies it with $H^0(\\mathbb P^3_\\mathbb C,F_0)$, where $F_0=F_A\\otimes_A\\mathbb C$. The image in $S_A$ of the map from the four coefficient copies of $U_A$ under $\\alpha_A$ is a direct summand and reduces to the corresponding coefficient-image subspace of $S_0$. For each real twistor line $\\ell$ in the reduced projective space, the restriction of $F_A$ to $\\ell_A=\\ell\\times_{\\mathbb C}\\operatorname{Spec}A$ is trivial of rank $N$, and reduction identifies its global sections with $H^0(\\ell,F_0|_\\ell)$. These conditions state the precise global, coefficient-image, and line-section base-change range; no arbitrary analytic family or algebraization assertion is included.\n\nExtend the coordinate map $j(\\lambda_1,\\lambda_2,\\mu_1,\\mu_2)=(-\\bar\\lambda_2,\\bar\\lambda_1,-\\bar\\mu_2,\\bar\\mu_1)$ semilinearly using the involution of $A$; write $\\widetilde\\sigma$ for its projective action over $A$ and $\\sigma$ for its reduction. Since $j^2=-1$, both projective actions square to the identity and preserve each real twistor line. A **real twistor line** means the projectivization of a $j$-invariant complex two-plane in $\\mathbb C^4$. Equivalently these are the finite lines\n$$\\mu_1=z_1\\lambda_1-\\bar z_2\\lambda_2,\\qquad \\mu_2=z_2\\lambda_1+\\bar z_1\\lambda_2,\\qquad (z_1,z_2)\\in\\mathbb C^2,$$\ntogether with $\\ell_\\infty=\\{\\lambda_1=\\lambda_2=0\\}$. Indeed a nonzero vector $v$ and $jv$ are complex-linearly independent because $j^2=-1$; they span the invariant plane. If its $\\lambda$ projection is nonzero, that projection and its quaternionic conjugate give an invertible two-by-two matrix with determinant $|\\lambda_1|^2+|\\lambda_2|^2$, so it has exactly the displayed graph form; if the projection is zero the plane is the $\\mu$ plane. Each fixed-line restriction above means the corresponding constant thickening $\\ell_A$.\n\nFor an $A$-locally free sheaf $G$, write $D_A(G):=(\\widetilde\\sigma^*\\overline G)^\\vee$, where $\\overline G$ has its scalar action conjugated by $a\\mapsto\\bar a$ and $(-)^\\vee=\\mathcal Hom_{\\mathcal O}(-,\\mathcal O)$. On the reduction, write $D(F_0):=(\\sigma^*\\overline{F_0})^\\vee$. A first-order real structure is an $\\mathcal O_{\\mathbb P^3_A}$-linear isomorphism $h_A:F_A\\to D_A(F_A)$ fixed by the canonical double-dual identification $D_A^2(F_A)\\cong F_A$. Its reduction $h_0:F_0\\to D(F_0)$ gives fiber pairings\n$$b_x(v,w):=h_{0,x}(v)(\\overline w),\\qquad v\\in(F_0)_x,\\quad w\\in(F_0)_{\\sigma x},$$\nwhich are linear in $v$, conjugate-linear in $w$, and satisfy $b_{\\sigma x}(w,v)=\\overline{b_x(v,w)}$. For a $\\sigma$-invariant real line $\\ell$ and $s,t\\in H^0(\\ell,F_0|_\\ell)$, the induced line form is the constant value of the function $x\\mapsto b_x(s(x),t(\\sigma x))$; constancy is part of the stated real-structure condition. It is first-slot-linear and Hermitian by the displayed symmetry. Positivity means $b_\\ell(s,s)>0$ for every nonzero $s$. A unitary framing at infinity is an isometric isomorphism $F_A|_{\\ell_\\infty}\\cong (A\\otimes_\\mathbb C W)\\otimes_A\\mathcal O_{\\ell_\\infty}$, where $\\ell_\\infty=\\{\\lambda_1=\\lambda_2=0\\}$ and $W=\\mathbb C^N$ has its standard first-slot-linear Hermitian form.\n\nAn isomorphism of such families is an $A$-linear chain isomorphism that intertwines the $\\sigma$-Hermitian pairings and the framing. No order or positivity is assigned to elements of $A$ with nonzero nilpotent part: positivity is required only after reduction.           "proof_strategy": "direct",
          "statement": "Let $k,N\\in\\mathbb Z_{\\ge0}$, and let $\\mathcal F$ be the locally free algebraic middle cohomology of a linear monad\n$$\n\\mathcal O_{\\mathbb P^3}(-1)^{\\oplus k}\\longrightarrow\\mathcal O_{\\mathbb P^3}^{\\oplus(2k+N)}\\longrightarrow\\mathcal O_{\\mathbb P^3}(1)^{\\oplus k}\n$$\non $\\mathbb P^3_\\mathbb C$, with exactness at both ends.\n\nFor algebraic sheaf cohomology, write $H^q(\\mathbb P^3,\\mathcal G)$ for the right-derived global-sections group. If these groups are finite-dimensional and vanish for all sufficiently large $q$, define the algebraic Euler characteristic by $\\chi(\\mathcal G)=\\sum_{q\\ge0}(-1)^q\\dim_{\\mathbb C}H^q(\\mathbb P^3,\\mathcal G)$. Let $H_{\\rm alg}=c_1^{\\rm alg}(\\mathcal O_{\\mathbb P^3}(1))$ in the Chow ring and let $H_{\\rm top}=c_1^{\\rm top}(\\mathcal O_{\\mathbb P^3}(1))$ in singular cohomology. The hyperplane cycle map $\\operatorname{cl}:A^1(\\mathbb P^3)\\to H^2(\\mathbb P^3;\\mathbb Z)$ identifies $H_{\\rm alg}$ with $H_{\\rm top}$; write $H$ for either class in the corresponding formula. The algebraic Chern character is $N-kH_{\\rm alg}^2$, the algebraic first Chern class is zero, the algebraic second Chern class is $kH_{\\rm alg}^2$, and the algebraic Euler characteristic is $N-2k$. The analytification of $\\mathcal F$ has total topological Chern class $1+kH_{\\rm top}^2$ through degree six and topological Chern character $N-kH_{\\rm top}^2$.\n\nLet $\\jmath:\\mathbb C^4\\to\\mathbb C^4$ be the conjugate-linear map\n$$\\jmath(\\lambda_1,\\lambda_2,\\mu_1,\\mu_2)=(-\\bar\\lambda_2,\\bar\\lambda_1,-\\bar\\mu_2,\\bar\\mu_1),\\qquad \\jmath^2=-1.$$\nUse $\\mathbb H=\\mathbb C\\oplus\\mathbb C\\mathbf j$, where $\\mathbf j^2=-1$ and $\\mathbf j a=\\bar a\\mathbf j$ for $a\\in\\mathbb C$, and identify $\\mathbb C^4$ with the right quaternionic vector space $\\mathbb H^2$ by\n$$ (\\lambda_1,\\lambda_2,\\mu_1,\\mu_2)\\longmapsto(\\lambda_1+\\bar\\lambda_2\\mathbf j,\\ \\mu_1+\\bar\\mu_2\\mathbf j).$$\nUnder this identification, right multiplication by $\\mathbf j$ is $\\jmath$. Give $\\mathbb H\\mathbb P^1=(\\mathbb H^2\\setminus\\{0\\})/\\mathbb H^\\times$ its standard smooth quotient structure; it is the 4-sphere and its points are the one-dimensional right-$\\mathbb H$ subspaces of $\\mathbb H^2$. The **quaternionic quotient map** is the smooth map\n$$\\pi:\\mathbb P(\\mathbb C^4)\\longrightarrow\\mathbb H\\mathbb P^1,\\qquad [\\lambda_1:\\lambda_2:\\mu_1:\\mu_2]\\longmapsto[(\\lambda_1+\\bar\\lambda_2\\mathbf j,\\ \\mu_1+\\bar\\mu_2\\mathbf j)]_{\\mathbb H}.$$\nEquivalently, $\\pi([v])=\\operatorname{span}_{\\mathbb C}(v,\\jmath v)$, a $\\jmath$-invariant complex two-plane. This is well-defined because $\\jmath(cv)=\\bar c\\,\\jmath v$ for $c\\in\\mathbb C$ and $v,\\jmath v$ are complex-linearly independent when $v\\ne0$ and $\\jmath^2=-1$. Its fiber over a quaternionic line $L$ is $\\mathbb P_{\\mathbb C}(L)\\cong\\mathbb P^1(\\mathbb C)$. In the finite chart with $\\lambda=\\lambda_1+\\bar\\lambda_2\\mathbf j\\ne0$ and $z=\\mu\\lambda^{-1}=z_1+\\bar z_2\\mathbf j$, the fiber equations are\n$$\\mu_1=z_1\\lambda_1-\\bar z_2\\lambda_2,\\qquad \\mu_2=z_2\\lambda_1+\\bar z_1\\lambda_2,$$\nand the fiber over the remaining point is $\\ell_\\infty=\\{\\lambda_1=\\lambda_2=0\\}$. Orient each fiber by its complex orientation. Write $z_1=x^0+ix^1$ and $z_2=x^2+ix^3$, so the chart orientation is $dx^0\\wedge dx^1\\wedge dx^2\\wedge dx^3$; orient $S^4$ so this positive stereographic chart followed by the fiber orientation induces the complex orientation of $\\mathbb P^3$. Since the base and fiber dimensions are $4$ and $2$, respectively, reversing these orientation factors has sign $(-1)^{4\\cdot2}=+1$, so this also agrees with the fiber-first convention. Let $u\\in H^4(S^4;\\mathbb Z)$ be the positive point class for this orientation. Then $\\pi^*u=H_{\\rm top}^2$.
